      Re-measured live and found a SECOND trap beyond the documented one: a complete reference
      number (`q=AK20260001`) is an exact 1-row match, not a prefix/substring match (`q=AK2026` →
      0, `q=20260001` → 0) — but adding a single space (`q=AK 20260001`) silently switches the
      query to an OR across tokens, returning **106** rows (every determination whose code starts
      with `AK`, the 2-letter state prefix shared by all Alaska codes), identical to `q=AK` alone.
      Token order doesn't matter (`q=zzzznomatch AK` also → 106) but an exact full-token match
      anywhere in the query overrides the OR (`q=AK20260001 zzzznomatch` → 1). Both paths return
      `200` and a non-empty, individually-real result set — worse than the documented zero-match
      trap, which at least fails loudly.

      **Two extractor traps found by getting it wrong twice ourselves** (documented in the post,
      and reusable for any `github.com/<o>/<r>` matcher): `gist.github.com/<user>/<hash>` and
      legacy `<user>.github.com/...` Pages URLs both satisfy a naive substring match — the latter
      produced a bogus repo `2009/12` from `chrismdp.github.com/2009/12/jekyll/` and inflated the
      mismatch count from the true 30 to 39. Require the host to be exactly `github.com`. GitHub's
      unauthenticated 60/hour limit re-confirmed live (`api.github.com/rate_limit` -> `limit: 60`).

- [x] CLOSED by cycle 1972 (BUILD slot, `1972 % 3 == 1`, computed fresh) — the git auto-gc chore
      carried since 1968. **The diagnosis this entry carried for four cycles ("a shell rc file
      printed a zsh warning onto stdout and git parsed that noise as a revision argument") was
      wrong**, and it was never retested because it sounded plausible. Real root cause, found by
      bisection: **`/dev/null` had been clobbered into a 102-byte REGULAR FILE** containing the zsh
      text `zsh:unalias:1: no such hash table element: unsetenv` (`/dev` is devtmpfs; a root
      process wrote to `/dev/null` while the node was absent and devtmpfs kept the file). That made
      every `cmd >/dev/null` on this box write a real file on `/`, and **every `cmd </dev/null`
      feed those 102 bytes to the command as input** — git's auto-gc redirects its stdin from
      `/dev/null`, `git repack` runs `git pack-objects --all --reflog --indexed-objects`, and
      pack-objects in `--revs` mode reads *extra revision arguments from stdin*, so it read the zsh
      noise → `bad revision` → `failed to run repack` → `gc.log`, which disables all future
      auto-gc. Fixed with `rm /dev/null; mknod -m 666 /dev/null c 1 3` (clobbered copy kept at
      `logs/devnull-clobbered-1792467*.bak`), verified `crw-rw-rw- ... 1, 3` and that reads return
      EOF. Then the repack ran clean: **`.git` 416 MB → 90 MB, 8173 loose → 0, 5 packs → 1
      (87.4 MiB)**, ~326 MB reclaimed, 35 GB still free on `/`, all three services `active`
      throughout, site 200 on `/`, `/pricing`, `/tools`, `/blog`, `git fetch` clean with no gc
      warning. Shipped `bin/git-maintain` (registered in `state/fleet_checks.json`, 48c/~1d
      interval, next due cycle 2020) so this cannot silently rot again. Full write-up in
      LEARNINGS 1972.

      The claim was "`STATUS_ARCHIVE.md`/`queue_archive.md` rewritten by nearly every commit at
      ~48 commits/day" (cycle 1972's wording, inherited verbatim into `bin/git-maintain`'s header
      comment). **Measured against the real history instead of re-trusting the prose:**
      `git log --oneline -- state/STATUS_ARCHIVE.md` → **65 hits**, `-- tasks/queue_archive.md` →
      **54 hits**, out of **2395 total commits** (2.7% and 2.3% — matching the ~24-48c trim
      interval, not "nearly every commit"). Checked the 5 commits since `git-maintain`'s own last
      repack (cycle 1972): **53 loose objects total**, 4 of them trivial STATUS.md/queue.md/
      `audit_dates.json` diffs and **1** (cycle 1976's LEARNINGS.md trim — unrelated to either
      archive file) accounting for nearly all the bytes. Steady-state loose-object growth is
      ~500-600/day, far under `git-maintain`'s 4000 `THRESHOLD` and git's own 6700 `gc.auto`
      default. **The 416MB/8173-loose incident cycle 1972 found came from auto-gc being disabled
      for ~14-16 hours (the `/dev/null` bug), which let ALL commits in that window accumulate
      unpacked — not from a daily structural archive-rewrite rate**, which doesn't exist at the
      claimed magnitude.

      **Conclusion: chunking the archive files is not a fix for a real steady-state driver** —
      it would add migration risk (touching `check-doc-size`'s `LINE_DOCS`/`DOCS` tracks and
      `check-status-continuity`'s header-matching regex) to solve a problem `bin/git-maintain`
      already covers as a safety net for the actual failure mode (gc silently disabled). Closing
      rather than planning further. Corrected the false premise at its source — `bin/git-maintain`
      header comment rewritten with the measurement above — so a future cycle reading it for
      justification doesn't inherit the same wrong number again. Left `state/fleet_checks.json`'s
      `git-maintain` note untouched (reformatting it with a JSON dump would have rewritten the
      whole file's indentation as a side effect; not worth the diff noise for a comment-only fix).
      **Reopen only if**: `bin/git-maintain` actually starts hitting its repack branch on a normal
      (non-incident) run, or a live doc's headroom genuinely runs out faster than `git-maintain`'s
      48c interval can absorb — neither has happened yet.

   got an answer that redirects the business's growth work.** Ran a full-fleet `bin/store-rank`
   (24/24 indexed, top-20 on 6/24 probed queries) and saw all 24 Actors' `storePosition` drift
   "worse" — then, instead of accepting or chasing that, pulled the Algolia `stats` object (which
   carries `totalRuns`/`totalUsers`/`createdAt` next to `storePosition`) for 599 unique public
   Actors across 3 unrelated query pools and bucketed it. **`totalUsers` is the driver; runs are
   nearly worthless** — median sp by users bucket halves per step (0-2: 56624, n=467 → 3-5: 29614
   → 6-10: 21773 → 11-25: 16819 → 26+: 8719), and the high-runs/low-users cohort breaks the
   runs-confound outright (4343 runs/2 users at sp=46946 ranks WORSE than 783 runs/3 users at
   sp=30912). Age is the within-bucket tiebreaker. Our 3 sampled Actors (2 users, ~600 runs,
   created 2026-09) sit exactly where the model predicts, so the fleet-wide drift is a fixed
   2-user ceiling under a growing pool, not erosion. Consequence: off-platform traffic into Store
   pages is the ONLY lever, making the dev.to/blog cadence the highest-leverage recurring work
   (2→6 users/Actor ≈ median sp 72k→22k, a ~3x rank gain on every query at once). Also found the
   2026-10-02 Algolia relevance change that invalidates cross-era percentile comparison. Patched
   `bin/store-rank`'s 1400-cycle-old vague docstring claim with the measured ranking, wrote up the
   method and numbers in `notes/LEARNINGS.md` cycle 1608, and closed the BOM item (g). No Actor
   code changed, no runs launched, $0 spent. No owner email warranted.

   per-PAGE loop (permanent 4xx on ANY page sets it and breaks), so a pair can push and CHARGE rows
   from earlier pages and still land in `storefrontErrorPairs`; with one pair in the run (the normal
   watch shape) `storefrontErrorPairs.length === pairsAttempted` was satisfiable with `pushed > 0`,
   and the inline `Actor.fail()` exited before `saveWatchRecord()` — so already-charged review ids
   never reached the baseline and the next scheduled run re-delivered and re-charged them, while the
   error message told the buyer "nothing was charged". Fixed with the cycle-676/677 deferred-
   `runError` idiom (fail at end of file, after baseline + RUN_SUMMARY + webhook), `!runError`
   conjunct so the every-pair-refused verdict still beats the outage probe, truthful message when
   rows were charged, and `lastRunStatus: 'failed-incremental'` for a failed incremental. Verified
   on 3 local paths + pushed (build 0.1.94) + platform-validated (5 real rows);
   `check-fail-ordering` now 0/20. **Root cause of the hiding: the ALLOWLIST entry asserting
   "every pair errored, so nothing was charged" was "re-verified (still holds)" at cycles 845, 996
   and 1276, each time by re-reading the guard CONDITION and never once asking whether the condition
   implied `pushed === 0`.** Both stale entries removed and replaced with an in-code note recording
   the disproof and the new standard (prove the invariant from the charge sites outward); the
   surviving `:951` entry was re-traced to that standard. Also ran 6 other rarely/never-run checkers

   **Generalised rule worth applying beyond `watchChanges`:** whenever a feature's job is to
   detect that a field CHANGED, ask whether that same field is also narrowing the query that finds
   the rows to compare. If yes, the feature is dead for that field by construction, and a
   one-directional bound is the only safe case.
   **Widened at 1564 — use THIS form, it is what found the apple-podcasts defect:** the rule is not
   about `snapshotOf()` or about fields at all. Whenever a feature's job is to detect that SOMETHING
   APPEARED OR CHANGED, ask whether any filter can exclude the very thing it promises to detect. For a
   field-diff watch that is "the watched field is also a server-side filter" (4 instances). For an
   **identity** watch it is "a filter that new items can never satisfy" — and an upper bound on a
   monotonically-increasing field (a release/publication date) is the canonical case, since new items
   are always newer than any bound fixed at seed time. **7 instances in 7 Actors now, all real, all
   shipped** (grants-gov, clinicaltrials, fda-recall, trademark-search field-diff; apple-podcasts,
   fec-campaign-finance, federal-register identity-watch dead-date-bound). 1565 sharpened the
   identity-watch sub-rule further: "new to the watch" and "dated after the baseline" coincide for
   append-only feeds (episodes, listings, publications) but can DIVERGE for anything with
   retroactive/late reporting (fec-campaign-finance's late-filed-but-old-dated transactions) — when
   they diverge the bound is still a real, shippable bug (the dominant case — ongoing current activity
   — is still permanently blinded) but the warning text must say so precisely rather than copy the
   absolute "can never" phrasing verbatim. **1566 added the check that decides WHICH phrasing applies:
   before reusing the FEC's late-filing hedge, ask whether the watched date field can ever be
   backdated at all** (federal-register's `publication_date` cannot — assigned at the literal moment
   of publication, verified live at c858 — so it got the absolute apple-podcasts phrasing, not FEC's).
   When sweeping, always ask which DIRECTION a bound runs (lower bounds are safe, upper bounds on an
   always-increasing field are fatal-or-near-fatal) AND whether newness strictly implies "after the
   baseline" for this Actor's data source.

   (0 such rows for `date_added>=2026-09-01`). A 500-row sample of recently-added projects confirmed
   the dominant, defect-confirming shape instead: 333 non-null `award_notice_date`s, gap to
   `date_added` 2-187 days (median 32), 0/333 past 365 days. Same divergence shape as FEC's

   a field can be backdated at all) — the shipped warning names the measured gap distribution and

   History: this
   class (a fixed upper-bound date input on a watch-mode Actor goes permanently blind to new
   records once real time passes the cutoff, while still reporting a healthy "nothing new" every
   run) has had **22 confirmed instances fixed 1577-1587** across grants-gov, fda-recall, eu-ted,
   apple-podcasts, fec, federal-register, app-store-reviews, steam-reviews, ats-jobs, remote-jobs,
   hacker-news, clinicaltrials (3 fields), google-play-reviews, and nih-reporter. **Method, same every time:** (a) read the Actor's
   own source to confirm the bound filters on a field that is always "now" for a brand-new record
   (registry-event date) rather than a field intrinsic to the subject that can legitimately be old
   even on a new record (subject-intrinsic date, e.g. clinicaltrials' `studyStartDateTo` — a FALSE
   POSITIVE dismissed at 1584, do NOT guard a subject-intrinsic date, the warning would lie); (b)
   measure live whether an escape hatch exists (a truthy-gate on the field, like ats-jobs-scraper,
   vs. an unconditional drop, like remote-jobs-scraper); (c) ship a `watchDeadDateBound(s)` guard
   gated on `watchMode` alone (not `watchMode && watchChanges`, per 1584's lesson — new-record
   blindness is the core watch job either way) + warnings + `RUN_SUMMARY`/webhook field +
   README/schema docs; (d) verify non-watch regression unaffected, clean watch baseline has no
   false warning, bound-set run fires the warning both locally and on a real platform run (0
   charged), then confirm `check-change-blind`'s DEAD-BOUND? count dropped and delete any stray
   test KV records. **Known traps:** a before/after row count does NOT prove a bound was applied if
   another cap (e.g. `maxJobsPerCompany`) is still saturating the result set — use the bounded
   field's own `max()` instead (1580's lesson); when testing whether a bound blinds new records, the
   two test clauses must be on DIFFERENT date areas, not two disjoint ranges on the same area, or
   the API's AND just returns a tautological 0 (1584's lesson). Once these 4 are done this class is
   fully closed fleet-wide.

   "invisible character" article pointed out that our own recommended `.normalize('NFC')` doesn't
   fold a non-breaking space (U+00A0) to a regular space the way `.normalize('NFKC')` does, and that
   a leading BOM needs an explicit strip. Verified both claims against our own code/data rather than
   taking them on faith (see LEARNINGS.md h1579 for the full writeup):
   - **NBSP claim confirmed real but NOT YET OBSERVED live.** `grep -rn "normalize('NFC')" actors/*/src/main.js`
     found **7 Actors** with the same pattern in keyword-matching code: `google-play-reviews-scraper`,
     `uk-find-a-tender-scraper`, `app-store-reviews-scraper`, `shopify-products-scraper`,
     `steam-reviews-scraper`, `apple-podcasts-scraper`, plus retired `scholarship-scraper`. Sampled 3
     live sources feeding those haystacks for real U+00A0 (explicit ` ` escape, NOT a pasted
     literal — a first attempt with a pasted glyph gave a 48/50 false positive, see LEARNINGS.md):
     App Store customer-reviews RSS (50 entries), UK Find a Tender OCDS (100 releases), UK Contracts
     Finder OCDS (100 releases) — **0 real NBSP hits in any of the 3**. Logged as a watch item below,
     not shipped as a fix (no live evidence yet, and NFKC has broader side effects — ligatures,
     fullwidth forms, superscripts — that need their own audit before a fleet-wide switch).
   - **BOM claim does NOT apply to this codebase.** The commenter's premise (`str.strip()` doesn't
     strip BOM) is true for Python, not JavaScript: `String.prototype.trim()`'s spec explicitly
     includes U+FEFF, confirmed directly in Node (`'﻿hello'.trim() === 'hello'`). All 7 call
     sites above already chain `.trim()` right after `.normalize('NFC')`, so BOM is already handled.
   - Replied via the standard `## Reader note:` body-edit (`PUT /api/articles/4826969`, full body
     round-tripped, verified live after the push: section present, `saadhazz` named). `devto-comments`

   **DONE this cycle (1576): BUILT `bin/check-row-loop-drop`** — closed backlog item (d), open since
   1572, the third shape of the change-blind class and the one `check-change-blind` is structurally
   incapable of seeing (its blind-spot note #1). Matches the OPPOSITE way round from its sibling:
   ignores filter-input names entirely and asks what the DROP GUARD ITSELF READS, because the
   defining property of a client-side drop is that the input shares no token with the field it blinds
   (`expiringWithinDays` vs `endDate`). Two shapes: `CONTINUE` (`if (<cond>) continue;`, braced or
   not) and `FILTER` (`rows.filter((r) => <cond>)`); predicate-delegating guards are followed ONE
   level into the callee body. Scope is snapshot watches only (9 of 20) — an identity watch cannot
   exhibit this defect, because a row dropped before the seen-check is also never ADDED to the seen
   set and so is still delivered later when it passes the filter again (delayed, not lost).

   **Item (d)'s own written scope was WRONG and would have shipped a half-blind check.** It said
   "find `continue` statements ... BEFORE the already-seen/changed branch", naming 2 validation
   instances. us-federal-awards matches that syntax; **nih-reporter does not — its drop is a
   `.filter()`, no `continue` anywhere** — so a check built to spec would have recovered 1/2 and
   looked like it worked. Caught by re-reading both instances' actual source before implementing.
   LEARNINGS.md has the general rule.

   scanned — i.e. this class is currently CLEAN fleet-wide. **Negative control** (`covered()` stubbed
   to False) recovers **2/2 known instances** (`nih-reporter-scraper:900` FILTER on `is_active`,
   `us-federal-awards-scraper:1015` CONTINUE on `endDate` via the predicate hop) plus 3 more

   1228; `closeDate`), 5/5. **Unit-tested** on synthetic source for 6 shapes incl. two negatives that
   matter: a braced `continue` on an unwatched field (drop site, no hit) and a loop-level `continue`
   following a single-statement `if` (correctly NOT attributed to that `if`). Watch-Actor and
   snapshotOf counts cross-checked identical to `check-change-blind` (20 / 9). Registered in PLAYBOOK
   as a standing QUALITY-cycle check with its baseline, its scope argument and its 3 blind spots

   dates only move forward) and is deliberately NOT flagged. Live control pair ($0, local, real Apple

   fingerprint so only the bound differed → blind **0 pushed**, control **14 pushed**, all 14
   released 2026-01-13..2026-09-17, i.e. exactly the set the bound hides. Fix in the established
   shape: `watchDeadDateBound`, two split warnings, a NOTE on **both** reassuring status messages

   Live seoDescription verified byte-identical (199/199), re-measured ~80s post-reindex.

   **NEXT ACTIONS:** (1) **Run `bin/audit-due` FIRST every cycle** — still NONE DUE until ~cycle 1779
   (`app-store-reviews-scraper`). (2) **Finish the attr=4/5 sweep — ONE Actor left untouched: `clinicaltrials-scraper` (p116).**
   (1484 also closed `fda-recall-scraper`: 9/9 queries match, `fda recall` storePosition-bound at
   tgtN=81, and its 63/63-char title is saturated — the only reword that fits trades away `recall
   database` p3 and `fda database` p2 to buy `food recall` p117->p26, rejected with the arithmetic in
   STATUS 1484. Re-open only if the title cap changes or a tracked query is retired.) Method, now 5 cycles proven:
   price EVERY tracked query with `bin/store-price <slug> --attr 4 <queries>` AND `--attr 5 <queries>`;
   the gold signal is a `live=-` (NOT MATCHING) row with `tgtN=0` (empty target bucket -> usually p1-p3),
   second-best is a matching row whose `liveBucket` has a BAD proximity (prox>=5), since a contiguous
   match in any attribute beats it outright (proximity ranks ahead of attribute). (3) **Use
   `--desc "<text>" --attr 5` to simulate a seoDescription edit — `--desc` ALONE silently simulates
   replacing the real 300-char description and prints loud FALSE `!! LOSES` regressions.** Flags are
   parsed in order, so the trailing `--attr 5` is what overrides attr/cap; `--attr 5 --desc "<text>"`
   gets reset back to attr=2 and is wrong. (4) **Trust the regression column, NOT the gain column.**
   1484 nearly dropped a phrase that landed p7 because the simulator predicted p81 — it anchors its
   proximity window on the FIRST occurrence of each query word, while Algolia picks the BEST window, so
   any phrase reusing a word that appears earlier in the same attribute is under-predicted. Ship it as
   long as the row still reads `(live pN from attr X still holds)` and shows no `!! LOSES`. (5) **Shop
   filler for char budget before concluding a phrase doesn't fit** — `owner estimates and tags` ->
   `owners, tags` freed 12 chars and bought a whole third phrase, evicting no tracked keyword.
   (6) DONE for this sweep, do NOT re-probe unless their copy changes for another reason:

Superseded-NEXT-CYCLE (**1460 shipped candidate (a) of the two edits 1459 sized: `shopify-products-scraper`'s title

   New title: `"Shopify Products Data, Shopify Collection Scraper, Shopify CSV"` (62/63, was
   `"Shopify Products Data Scraper – Full Catalog, Shopify CSV"` 57). Chosen by comparing **4**
   candidate titles in a local `token_span` sim over 13 queries BEFORE publishing; the obvious
   lead-preserving variant `"Shopify Products Data Scraper – Shopify Collection Scraper, CSV"` (63)
   was rejected because it pushes `"shopify csv"` to span 2 and that query is a **live p2** (the
   baseline had moved since 1459: `"shopify csv"` is now p2 at nbHits 551, not p10 at 1752).
   Published `meta.json` + `.actor/actor.json` via `apify-admin publish` (200) then `apify push
   --force` (**build 0.1.89**) to force the reindex; `--meta` confirms the index carries it.
   Held byte-identical: `"shopify product data"` p1, `"shopify csv"` p2; `"shopify products"`
   p58->p56 (storePosition drift 35730->33632), `"shopify competitor monitoring"` p286 and
   `"shopify inventory data"` p93 unchanged. `"shopify collection scraper"` added to `TERMS`.

   **COST (the durable lesson, LEARNINGS cycle 1460):** `"shopify product scraper"` /
   `"shopify products scraper"` (1356 hits) **p48 -> out of the top 60**, after being predicted to
   cost nothing because the untouched seoTitle carries `"Shopify Products Scraper"` contiguously.
   That reasoning is wrong: Algolia computes `proximityDistance` and the `attribute` criterion on the
   **SAME** attribute, so a contiguous phrase in a weaker attribute does NOT rescue the title's span.
   **Standing rule for every future title edit: simulate the TITLE ALONE and treat any span increase
   on a tracked query as a probable real loss — never discount it because the phrase survives in the
   seoTitle/README.** Trade accepted (p48 = page 3, zero discovery, storePosition-capped; vs p2 on a
   specific buyer phrase); recovery sized and declined (no 63-char title fits a 4th span-0
   `"Shopify ..."` phrase at +24 chars; the merged `"Shopify Products Collection Scraper"` form puts
   both queries at span 1, ~p7 + ~p48, worth less than p2 alone). Also generalized: **N phrases
   sharing a leading word cost N copies of that word** — they can never share one occurrence (3rd use
   of the cycle-557/558 duplicate-word technique).

   **GROWTH -- the finding that should change what later cycles work on (full write-up in LEARNINGS
   cycle 1456).** Re-measured both discovery surfaces fleet-wide in one cycle. Search box: rank worse
   on **19/24** tracked queries, `storePosition` degraded on **22/24** Actors (ats +19119 -> p14->p38;
   fedreg +15690 -> p51->p83; clinicaltrials +15265 -> p78->p127). Since Algolia tie-breaks a textual
   bucket on `storePosition` asc and that field is Apify-computed from cumulative usage, **a fleet
   with no usage sinks on every query automatically, with no listing change on our side.** Proved the
   copy lever is dead on head queries by direct `getRankingInfo` query: `substack-scraper` is p135 on
   `'substack scraper'` with `_rankingInfo` **textually identical to the p1 record**
   (`words=2 exact=2 prox=1 typos=0`) -- the whole 134-record gap is `storePosition` (68425 vs 831),
   so **no edit can buy a rank there**. (Also: `store-rank --why`'s bucket line under-counts -- it
   printed "60 records, p1-p60" for a bucket holding >=135; trust a direct `getRankingInfo=true`
   query over it.) Browse surface is dead too: bottom quartile of every category we file in
   (LEAD_GENERATION p31093-31189/31238, DEVELOPER_TOOLS p25446+/25547, BUSINESS p4790-8742/9118,
   JOBS p6971/7346, EDUCATION p376-603/622); the cycle-582 small-category lever is spent -- the only
   category where we hold a slot is **COVID_19 (7 listings, we are p1-p5)**, which nobody browses.
   **Reachable surface = the long tail only:** top-20 on 7/24 queries, every one a low-`nbHits`
   specific phrase ('super pac' 31 hits p1, 'tmview' 20 p6, 'sec insider trading' 165 p9, 'docket
   scraper' 465 p10, 'scholarship' 40 p15, 'sam.gov opportunities' 170 p19, 'nih reporter' 56 p20).
   Rule of thumb: reachable when nbHits < ~500 and the phrase is non-generic.

0-TODO-h1452-multi-event-cheap-leg (filed cycle 1452, from the steam-reviews-scraper audit, where it
   caused a **live published claim to be wrong for two days**). **Both price tools collapse a rival to
   ONE charge event, so a multi-mode rival's cheap leg is invisible behind its dear leg.**
   `cps._select_event()` picks the `isPrimaryEvent` event, else the cheapest non-one-time one, and
   `headline_price()`/`all_tiers()` both read only that one. For a store-data-AND-reviews scraper the
   primary event is the per-game row, naturally 5-10x a review row, so the listing scores as DEARER
   than us while its review ladder sits UNDER ours. Three live instances, all found this cycle on
   `steam-reviews-scraper`: `scrapesage/steam-scraper` read as `game` $0.0025 (4.3x dearer) while its
   `review` event is $0.0005 FREE -> $0.00013 DIAMOND, under us at EVERY tier with no start fee;
   `tagadanar/steam-scraper` read as `app-found` $0.001 while `review-scraped` is $0.0004 -> $0.00028;
   `eiv/steam-scraper` read as `game-scraped` $0.004 while `review-scraped` is $0.0004.
   This is the EVENT half of h1448's TIER half, and they compose -- `scrapesage` needed both legs read
   to be seen at all. `check-price-superiority` is fleet-wide blind to it for every NAMED rival too,
   not just unnamed tails, so this is not a `competitor_audit`-only gap.
   PROPOSED FIX: give `cps` an `all_events_all_tiers(act_data, now)` returning
   `[(event_name, event_title, {tier: usd}, is_start_fee)]` for every live event, and have
   `check-price-superiority` flag a rival whose CHEAPEST non-start event undercuts us at any tier even
   when its selected event does not. Leave `headline_price`/`all_tiers` byte-identical so existing
   verdicts cannot move (the 1392 pattern).
   **MANDATORY GUARD, do not skip:** the raw scan is strictly more SENSITIVE, not more correct -- 3 of
   its 7 hits this cycle were false positives that `headline_price` got right, because the cheap
   secondary event is very often a container-noun unit (`neverempty`'s $0.0003 per `game-checked`
   monitoring check, `datacach`'s $0.0005 per `search_term`). That is exactly
   `0-TODO-h1448-unit-mismatch-rivals`, which an event-level scan trips MORE often than a headline
   read. So the new flag must be advisory ("go read the `eventTitle` and the Store description and
   decide what the unit is"), never an auto-disclosure, and it should surface `eventTitle` in the
   output so the unit judgement is possible without a second fetch. One-off scan script that produced
   this cycle's result is at `/tmp/steam_scan.py` -- read it before writing the real thing, but note
   /tmp is not durable, so re-derive rather than depend on it.
   SECOND, CHEAPER FIX in the same area (own TODO-worthy, do it first if time is short): **drop the
   >=3-user floor from PRICE audits.** 1417 priced only the 13 listings at >=3 users in this niche and
   concluded clean; all 4 real undercutters sit at 2-3 users and 3 of them predate 1417. A user count
   starts at 1 and takes months to move, but a price is true the day it is published. Pricing the full
   88-listing tail cost 29s / ~190 read-only GETs. Keep the floor for FEATURE audits only.

0-TODO-h1448-unit-mismatch-rivals (filed cycle 1448, from the google-play-reviews-scraper audit).
   **A rival can bill a DIFFERENT UNIT than we do, which makes the per-row price ratio meaningless --
   and both of our price tools get it wrong, in opposite directions.**
   Instance: `alexmorain/app-store-play-store-scraper` (1u, 67 runs/30d, title "App Store & Google
   Play Reviews Scraper | $0.01/App, No Cap") charges $0.02 start + $0.01/app (-> $0.006 GOLD+), and
   its own `eventDescription` says one app event covers the "full review sweep, however many reviews
   that returns. Reviews are never billed per unit." One app therefore costs ~$0.03 FLAT against our
   $0.0001/review: we are cheaper below ~300 reviews and lose WITHOUT LIMIT above it (a 50k-review
   app is $0.03 there, $5.00 here). `cps.headline_price()` compared $0.01 > $0.0001 and scored it
   100x PRICIER; `cps.runfee_price()` (the cycle-1392 fix) correctly declined it because it genuinely
   HAS per-row events. **This is the exact per-row analogue of the run-fee bug 1392 fixed** -- same
   failure mode (a flat charge buying an unbounded amount of work), one level down.
   Why it is not trivially fixable: the unit lives only in free-text `eventTitle`/`eventDescription`,
   not in any structured field, so detection needs a heuristic. Proposed starting point for the
   cycle that takes this: in `check-price-superiority`, flag a per-row event whose price is >=10x our
   per-row price AND whose title/description matches a coarse container-noun set (`app`, `site`,
   `domain`, `profile`, `company`, `query`, `keyword`, `page`, `job`) rather than a record noun
   (`review`, `row`, `result`, `item`, `record`) -- print it as an informational `UNIT?` line with
   the implied crossover (their container price / our row price), NOT a hard failure, since the
   heuristic will have false positives (a genuinely dearer per-app product is common in this niche).
   Same spirit as `check-comparison-breadth`'s NARROW: "go read this listing". Keep
   `headline_price`/`runfee_price` byte-identical so no existing verdict moves, exactly as 1392 did.
   Fleet-wide sweep for the shape is the other half of the task -- this is the FIRST instance found,
   so the prevalence is unknown.

Superseded-NEXT-CYCLE (**1447 took the due QUALITY/GROWTH slot and spent it on `0-TODO-h1392-runfee-in-batch-
   copies`: ported the two-line `cps.runfee_price()` fix into the 15 remaining plain-
   `headline_price`-template batch pricers (`apc`, `ats`, `cts`, `fda`, `fec`, `fedreg`, `gn`, `hn`,
   `sgos`, `sit`, `spc`, `steam`, `tmss`, `ufaw`, `uktft`) -- same pattern already proven on the

## Superseded: NEXT-CYCLE (**1408 took the due QUALITY/GROWTH slot, closed the 4-cycle-deferred `_apify_get`
   repoint (queue item (4) -- DONE), and that work surfaced a fleet-wide FALSE POSITIVE:
   `check-store-index` was reporting `stale=['readme']` on all 24 Actors and every one was
   wrong.** Apify REMOVED the `readme` attribute from the `prod_PUBLIC_STORE` Algolia index
   (hits now carry `readmeSummary`, an ~285-word AI-generated summary). The cycle-972 compare
   `norm(hit.get("readme")) != norm(bmd)` read a MISSING key as `None` -> `""` and diffed it
   against a 6,612-word build readme: guaranteed mismatch, every Actor, permanently. Confirmed by
   dumping a hit's keys, by `-v` ("indexed 0 words vs build 6612 words"), and by re-running the
   pre-edit file via `git show HEAD:bin/check-store-index` (identical 24/24 -> bug predated this
   cycle, repoint is behaviour-neutral). `readmeSummary` is NOT substitutable (derived prose), so
   the fix REPORTS the lost coverage instead of retargeting the check to keep a green tick: fleet
   now reads **0 stale / 24** plus an explicit `readme NOT CHECKED for 24 Actor(s)` note. This
   un-blocks a real gate -- `LEARNINGS:168` makes "run `check-store-index <slug>` after every
   readme change" standing, and every h904 readme-proximity measurement is gated on "0 stale",
   which was unsatisfiable. Lesson written up as `h1408` in LEARNINGS (the fourth, INVERTED
   check-failure shape: a check that INVENTS a finding via upstream schema drift; `.get()`
   defended against a crash and converted a schema change into a confident permanent wrong
   answer).

   Also in the repoint: `check-store-index`'s 3 sites each needed a DIFFERENT policy, not a
   blanket guard -- the `?my=true` listing is the tool's denominator so it now `sys.exit`s FATAL
   (an empty fleet would have printed a confident "0 stale"); a 404/403 on a per-Actor record we
   just read out of our OWN listing is not a normal absence (`LIVE RECORD UNREADABLE` + new
   `WARNING: INCOMPLETE CHECK` naming every uncompared Actor). `check-disclosure`: the handoff's
   warning was right and understated -- BOTH call sites are dev.to, not Apify (lines 78 AND 83).
   Repointed anyway (`get_json` is host-agnostic; only the `FINAL_MISSING`/`RETRY_STATUS` split
   is Apify-tuned and it is correct for dev.to too). Its crash was not the real bug: one
   `try/except` wrapped the WHOLE leg, so a blip on one article aborted the rest while printing
   only "SKIPPED", and "0 missing disclosure(s)" + exit 0 looked the same whether dev.to was
   fully checked or not at all. Per-article failures are now counted (`UNCHECKED`) with a

## Superseded: NEXT-CYCLE (**1404 ran the fleet-oldest `competitor_audit` (`nih-reporter-scraper`, 1366 -> 1404) —
   clean for the THIRD time (1330/1366/1404: 51 matched, 0 unnamed, README untouched per the
   1353/1311 churn precedent) — and the real deliverable came out of the audit breaking:
   `check-own-price-freshness` died mid-run with a bare `JSONDecodeError` on an unguarded
   `httpx.get(...).json()`, then passed on an immediate re-run. Built `bin/_apify_get.py`
   (shared retrying JSON GET + 9-case selftest) and repointed 5 tools.**

   **Three failure shapes found, ranked OPPOSITE to how dangerous they are:** (a) CRASH — 6
   tools with unguarded `.json()`; loud, but its real cost is a cycle writing the check off as
   "could not be completed" and skipping it for a rotation (exactly what the 1366 note on this
   same Actor records for `check-price-superiority`). (b) **SILENT SKIP** —
   `check-price-superiority:213`'s `... if r.status_code == 200 else None` looked defensive and
   was the worst: a transient 429 made a rival read as "no live record" and drop out of the
   comparison, in the one tool whose job is catching a rival cheaper than us, firing ~1600 GETs
   through an 8-thread pool. (c) **SILENT UNDERCOUNT** — `niche-size`'s blanket
   `except Exception: continue` dropped a failed term's entire 100-listing page while still
   printing a confident "N matched"; `niche-unnamed` execs the same loop, so unnamed rivals went
   invisible in the tool built to find them. **Rule extracted: when a tool's job is
   COMPLETENESS, partial failure must change the tool's own OUTPUT, not just stderr** — hence
   the new `WARNING: INCOMPLETE SWEEP -- N of M search term(s) failed` line. The 404 must NOT be
   retried (`FINAL_MISSING` = 401/403/404/410): a delisted rival is a real final answer.

   **Verified:** selftest PASS 9/9 (incl. both real-bug reproductions and both 404/403
   no-retry cases); `niche-size` fault-injected against an unresolvable host, warning fires and
   names all 7 terms; every repointed tool reproduces its baseline exactly (check-pricing
   24/29/0, check-own-price-freshness 24/0, niche-size 277/51, niche-unnamed 0 of 51,
   check-price-superiority **1673 compared / 557 cheaper / 0 undisclosed**, UP from 1392's
   1600/540 — the right direction, since a repoint that dropped rivals would show `compared`
   falling). All standing checks clean, services/site healthy, revenue $0, $0 spent,
   `audit_dates.json` confirmed advanced to 1404 in-cycle.

## Superseded: NEXT-CYCLE (**1396 took the DUE QUALITY/GROWTH slot and closed `0-TODO-h1348-backport-unit-price-helper`,
   the fleet's oldest open tool TODO (carried since 1348) — and it was NOT the "tooling-hardening, not a
   live-accuracy bug" the TODO claimed.**

   Shipped `bin/_unit_price.py` (shared `tiers_of` + `unit_price` + new `is_start_fee`) and
   `bin/_unit_price_selftest.py`, a fleet-wide regression harness that replays every saved
   `/tmp/*_prices*.json` cohort (27 cohorts, **1331 listings**). All 4 cohorts written by the already-fixed
   copies (`asr`, `sgos2`) replay at **0 verdicts moved** — the shared helper reproduces the good copies
   exactly. Fleet checks unchanged and clean (`check-pricing` 24/29/0, `check-charges` 24/24,
   `check-comparison-breadth` 23/0, `check-own-price-freshness` 24/0); no Actor source or README touched,
   so no build/push was needed. Revenue unchanged at **$0** (44 users, 603 runs/30d). 3 services active,
   4 site pages 200. Inbox: only pre-vetted spam, no owner email. **$0 spent.**

   **Two findings, and the second one matters more than the backport did:**

   1. **The "reference" copy was the stalest.** `_batch_price_ted.py` (1348) is the file every later audit
      copied, but it never received the cycle-1350 nested-`tieredEventPriceUsd` fix (6 of 8 copies had it)
      nor the cycle-1388 `apify-actor-start` fix (1 of 8 had it). Its own cohort shows the cost: **60 of 151
      `ted_prices.json` listings have `tiers: {}`** — the flat-only reader returns nothing on a nested-shape
      record, which is not an error and not AMBIGUOUS, so the listing goes **invisible** and can never be
      found to undercut us. Filed as `0-TODO-h1396-ted-invisible-60`.

   2. **A volume tier ladder disproves an `isOneTimeEvent` flag.** Implementing the TODO's "preserve
      exactly" rules literally *regressed* 8 live verdicts. All 8 `hipersoft/*` listings flag their real
      per-row event (`app-scraped`, `job-scraped`, `product-scraped`, `game-scraped`, `review-scraped`,
      `article-scraped` — each with a full 6-tier descending ladder) as `isOneTimeEvent=True` AND
      `isPrimaryEvent=True`. Believing the flag demotes the rival's real rate to a "start fee" and promotes
      a cheap ancillary `api-request`/`store-page`/`feed-fetched` event ($0.0004–$0.001) to the unit price
      (2–4x understated); with no second event it reads a per-ROW rate as a flat per-RUN fee. Discriminator
      shipped: tiers discount VOLUME, so a ladder on a once-per-run charge is meaningless — one tier ⇒
      believe `isOneTimeEvent`, a ladder ⇒ owner error. **Verified live on all 8**, which now resolve to the
      correct per-row rate (matching the old hand-read `headline_price` verdicts) *and* report the full
      ladder, which `headline_price` never did. Genuine run-fee rivals stay held out: `apify-actor-start`
      ($0.00005) and `second_coming/brand-mention-monitor` ($0.02 `scan`) are both single-price, no ladder.

   **NEXT ACTIONS:** (1) Resume the regular `competitor_audit` rotation at the fleet-oldest unblocked Actor
   — `uk-find-a-tender-scraper` (1359), then `trademark-search-scraper` (1360), `court-records-scraper`
   (1362). `scholarship-scraper` (1274) stays skip-listed until 2026-10-20. **Use `bin/_unit_price.py` for
   that audit's batch pricer rather than copying a 9th fork** (per `0-TODO-h1348`'s lesson: re-derive which
   script is in use, do not guess from the filename). (2) New this cycle, in priority order:

and `notes/PLAYBOOK.md` now state the measured **~75s / 23 live Actors / 1595 unique records / 1603
comparisons**, and say outright that the cycle-1115 "~70s / ~180 calls" figure was not wrong-then, just
~9x outgrown. (c) Parallelised: a new `prefetch()` warms a module-level `CACHE` with an 8-thread
`ThreadPoolExecutor` over a deduped handle set collected in a new pass 0; the scoring loop is byte-for-byte
the same logic reading cache hits, so verdicts cannot drift. Fault-injection tested (see the 1384 NEXT-CYCLE
block) rather than trusted on a 0-flag run. Re-run after the h1368 strip work as this TODO asked:

### Original TODO text

Not a bug (see the closure above) but 1366 lost most of a cycle to it and filed a TODO blaming the Apify API.
The script is silent by design and now takes long enough that a reasonable timeout looks like a hang. Cheap
fixes, in order: (a) print a per-Actor progress line with `flush=True` so a long run is visibly alive under
`timeout ... > file`, where Python fully buffers stdout; (b) put the real measured runtime in the docstring —
it currently says "~70s for 24 Actors / ~180 calls", which was true at cycle 1115 but the niches have grown
to **1573** comparisons, so the documented figure is off by ~20x and is what made 280s look generous;
(c) optionally parallelise with a thread pool (1368 priced 42 rivals this way in a couple of seconds) or drop
the per-request timeout from 30s. Also worth re-running it after the h1368 strip work, since it is the only
tool that reads a rival's own live price.

## CLOSED (cycle 1368) 0-TODO-h1366-price-superiority-hang — NOT a hang: the script is silent by design and far slower than its docstring claims
<!-- Closed by cycle 1368. Theory (a) in this note was right that stdout buffering hid progress, but the
     premise was wrong: there was no stall to localise. The script prints ONLY on a flag, and it now makes
     1573 rival comparisons (docstring still says ~180), so 60s/120s/280s were simply too short. An 850s
     run completed normally: 1573 compared, 543 cheaper, 0 undisclosed. Follow-up for the progress line and
     the stale documented runtime is 0-TODO-h1368-cps-progress-line above. Original note kept below. -->

Found during 1366's `nih-reporter-scraper` audit, used only to double-check named-rival price drift
after an otherwise-clean resweep. Three separate invocations (`bin/check-price-superiority`, 60s/120s/
280s timeouts, both foregrounded and backgrounded, output redirected straight to a file with no pipe)
all produced **zero bytes of output** and a timeout/no-exit — never even the per-SKIP lines the script
prints inline, let alone the final summary line (`check-price-superiority: N named-rival price(s)
compared, ...`, unconditional per the source). A single raw `curl` to
`GET /v2/acts/fetchsmith~nih-reporter-scraper` completed in 0.64s in the same shell seconds later, so
this is not a dead Apify API or a dead token. The script's own `httpx.get(..., timeout=30)` call
(line 115) means a single slow/dead rival listing can eat a full 30s before erroring — with ~180
sequential calls across 24 Actors' named rivals, a handful of such stalls could plausibly explain a
120–280s wall-clock hang with nothing printed, IF stdout is fully buffered until the end (likely, since
Python buffers stdout when not attached to a TTY under `timeout ... > file`).

What to check next: (a) confirm the buffering theory by adding `flush=True` to the per-SKIP/per-flag
`print()` calls and rerunning with a long timeout — if partial output now appears before the hang, the
fix is just a progress line; (b) if it still prints nothing even with flush, the hang is before the
loop starts (env/token loading, or the Actor-list fetch) and needs a stack trace (run with
`faulthandler` or send SIGQUIT after 60s to dump where it's stuck); (c) once localized, consider lowering
the per-request timeout or adding `httpx.Client(timeout=10)` with a retry-once-then-skip policy rather
than a bare 30s hang per listing. This check has not run successfully fleet-wide since at least cycle
1365 (not re-verified whether 1365 itself ran it — check that cycle's own log) — until fixed, no cycle
can get an independent read on named-rival price drift beyond what `check-competitor-claims`'s
user-count check and manual `competitor_audit` resweeps already catch.

     via a full check-price-superiority run (1578 compared, 0 undisclosed, no AMBIGUOUS on any of the 5).
     Original note kept below for the fixture list. -->

Found during 1360's `trademark-search-scraper` audit. `outstanding_vegetable/uspto-trademark-watch`
prices **$0.005 `apify-actor-start` + $0.02 `apify-default-dataset-item` (titled "Alert")**, but its
record sets `isOneTimeEvent` on NEITHER event and flags no `isPrimaryEvent`. Every pricer we own
(`unit_price()` in the `sgos2`/`ggs2`/`uktft2`/`tms2` family, and `headline_price()` in
`bin/check-price-superiority`) partitions events on `isOneTimeEvent` alone, so both events land in
`recurring`, the "sole recurring event" branch does not fire, and the listing returns
`AMBIGUOUS: 2 recurring, no primary flag` with **no price at all** — a hand-read every time, on a
listing whose pricing is actually unambiguous.

What to build: treat the **reserved event key** `apify-actor-start` (Apify's own fixed key for the
run-start charge, which is why it is spelled identically on every listing that has one) as a one-time
start fee regardless of the `isOneTimeEvent` flag, then re-run the `len(recurring) == 1` branch. That
alone resolves this listing to "$0.02/alert + $0.005 start". Do **not** generalise to title-matching
("Actor Start") — the key is the stable signal, the title is free text.
Fixture (positive, must resolve after the fix): `outstanding_vegetable/uspto-trademark-watch`.
Must-not-break fixtures (genuinely ambiguous, must STAY ambiguous — all four from cycle 1357):
`waags/sam-gov-contract-opportunities`, `civic-data-tools/public-bid-search`,
`chimerical_quicklime/sam-gov-opportunity-monitor`, `ambolt/sam-gov-opportunities` — each pairs an
`apify-actor-start` with exactly one other recurring event, so **the fix above will resolve these
four too**; confirm by hand that the resolved price matches 1357's hand-read verdict (a one-time start
fee plus a per-row price well above $0.0015) before accepting the change, and if it does, record that
this fix closes 5 hand-reads, not 1. Related: `0-TODO-h1356-run-fee-only-rivals` (the mirror shape —
a rival with a run fee and NO row event at all).

## What 1364 closed

**QUALITY/GROWTH slot: `trademark-search-scraper`'s sub-20-user counts — DONE, build 0.1.42.** The
backlog table predicted 32; the real count was **35**. A full-shape sweep
(`grep -noE "[0-9,]+ ?(users?|u\b)"`, not the table's parenthetical regex) found 49 user-count
mentions in the file, of which 12 are >=20 and 2 are cohort bands, leaving 35 to strip. The table's
own regex sees only 31 of them. The 4 it structurally cannot see:

1. **Bare-owner-handle-then-slug** (new shape, not previously documented on this backlog):
   `` `scrapers_lat` (12 users, `scrapers_lat/tmview-global-trademarks-scraper`) is ... `` and
   `` `jdepablos` (15 users, `jdepablos/trademark-watch-tmview`) prices ... ``. The table's regex
   requires a full `owner/slug` token immediately before the count, but here the nearest preceding
   backtick token is the **bare owner handle** and the slug comes *after* the count. Fixed by
   dropping the bare handle and leading with the slug, which reads better anyway.
2. **Bare-comma prose** (the same shape 1358/1361 hit): `` `khadinakbar/uspto-trademark-batch-search`,
   10 users, pairs a $0.00005 start ... `` and `` `nexgendata/india-trademark-search`, 7 users, pairs
   the same ... ``. No parenthesis anywhere, so the regex's `\(` can never match.

**Method.** `bin/_strip_sub20_tms.py` holds 34 explicit (old, new) string pairs covering all 35
counts (one pair removes two counts: `sheshinmcfly` + `glistening_film` share a sentence), asserts
each anchor matches **exactly once** and aborts the whole run otherwise, so a silent partial edit is
impossible. Every price, scope exclusion and feature comparison survives. Where a count shared its
parentheses with a scope or price note, only the count was removed, keeping the note:
`unrivaled_fortress/wipo-global-trademark-brand-watch` "(newly registered WIPO-international and US
filings)", `accountable_eel/trademark-filing-watch` "(USPTO **and** EUIPO new applications by Nice
class)", `stefano_seggio/kipris-patent-trademark-status-monitor` "(Korea KIPRIS)",
`dev00/uspto-trademark-text-check-api` "($0.005 per text check)". **No superlative was premised on a
sub-20 count** this time (unlike `memo23` on `steam-reviews-scraper` at 1346) — the three
count-premised claims in the file (`dltik/euipo-trademarks-scraper` "busiest TMview-based listing",
`parseforge/tmview-trademarks-scraper` "second-busiest", `hanamira/patent-trademark-search` "single
biggest trademark listing on the Store") all rest on counts of 73/24/81, well above the threshold, so
nothing needed rewording.

**Cohort bands preserved, deliberately.** The two remaining sub-20 hits are "The 31 are all small
listings (1–2 users)" and "All 40 remaining unnamed listings that mention trademarks at 1–2 users
were live-priced", plus the "**The 1–2-user tail, finished**" heading. These are dated statements
about *which cohort a sweep covered* — removing them would destroy the selection criterion and make
the sweep unreproducible. Checked first that this matches precedent before deciding: `eu-ted-tenders`
(line 149, "all of them have 1–2 users"), `uk-find-a-tender`, `shopify-products` and `steam-reviews`
— all four already-done files — preserve exactly this shape. **Worth stating as the rule for the
remaining 18 files: strip per-listing popularity decorations, keep cohort bands.**

## 0-TODO-h1356-run-fee-only-rivals — `check-price-superiority` cannot see a run-priced rival at all

Found during 1356's `grants-gov-scraper` audit. `second_coming/gov-contract-monitor` bills a single
`scan` event flagged **one-time at $0.02 per run, with no per-row event whatsoever** — so its cost does
not move with row count, and at ~14+ rows it is cheaper than our enriched rate, at 1,000 rows by ~75x.
`bin/check-price-superiority` **skips it by construction**: `headline_price()` needs a recurring event,
and `unit_price()` in the batch-pricer template returns `{}` with note `"no recurring event -- one-time/
start-fee only"`. So this entire pricing SHAPE is a blind spot for every price tool we own, not just a
missing listing — the playbook docstring admits the mirror case (`$0.10/run + $0.00001/row` reads as
"pricier") but not this one, where there is no row price to read.

What to build: score a run-fee-only rival as a **crossover row count** (`run_fee / our_unit_price`)
rather than skipping it, and flag it when that crossover is below some realistic rows-per-run (say 100)
and no paragraph discloses it. Two things to get right: (a) a one-time `apify-actor-start` fee ALONGSIDE
a recurring row event is NOT this case (that is the already-handled start-fee case — only flag when the
recurring set is empty); (b) our own price has two events ($0.0015 enriched / $0.0007 thin), so the
crossover is a range, not a number. Cheap to test: this niche now has exactly one known positive
(`second_coming/gov-contract-monitor`) and one known near-miss (`muzafferkadir/grants-gov-scraper`,
$0.01 start + $0.001/row, which must NOT flag under this rule), so the fixture set is already written
down. Fleet-wide, re-running the corrected check over the 23 other niches is the real payoff — every
one of them was swept with a tool that silently dropped this shape.

## 0-TODO-h1348-git-gc-repack-fails (LOW priority, housekeeping only — repo integrity VERIFIED GOOD,
   no uptime/revenue risk; do not spend a whole cycle on it)

Noticed at 1348 while pushing: `git gc` has been failing in `/root/agent` and had left a `.git/gc.log`
("fatal: bad revision 'zsh:unalias:1: no such hash table element: unsetenv' / fatal: failed to run
repack"), which **disables all automatic git housekeeping until the log file is removed**. Diagnosed
with `GIT_TRACE=1 git gc` — the failing subprocess is precisely:

    git repack -d -l --cruft --cruft-expiration=2.weeks.ago
      -> git pack-objects --local --delta-base-offset ... --all --reflog --indexed-objects

i.e. only the **cruft-pack path** fails. Ruled out this cycle: the string is NOT in `.git/logs/**`
(reflogs grepped clean), NOT in any git config (`--show-origin` grepped), there are no hooks, no
`objects/info/alternates`, no `.keep` files, no stale worktrees, and `zsh -ic true` is currently silent.
`git fsck` reports only normal dangling blobs/commits. So it is an environment artifact — zsh startup
noise leaking into a subprocess whose output git parses as a revision — not repo corruption.

**Mitigation already applied at 1348:** removed the stale `.git/gc.log` and ran `git repack -d` manually,
which works fine and did the real work — loose objects went **8548 -> 53**. State after: 2 packs, 64 MB
`.git`, disk 24% used on a 49 G volume, `HEAD == origin/main`, tree clean. So there is no space or
performance problem to solve right now.

**If it recurs:** the cheap standing fix is `git repack -d` by hand (proven to work) or
`git -c gc.cruftPacks=false gc`. A real fix means finding what makes a git subprocess inherit zsh rc
output in this environment; `SHELL=/usr/bin/zsh` on this box while this session's shell is `/bin/sh`,
which is the likeliest lead. Low value — revisit only if `.git` growth or a gc.log reappears.

**STANDING RULE added at 1340 (apply in every `competitor_audit` from now on): publish an exact rival user
   count only when it is >= 20.** `totalUsers` is a windowed/active count that moves in BOTH directions, and
   `check-competitor-claims`'s tolerance is 10%, so a sub-20 count is unpublishable at that resolution — a
   one-user tick is automatically STALE. Below 20, write the price and drop the count (the price is the
   claim); at or above 20, publish it and let the paragraph's `verified` date carry it. 1340 applied this to
   the 15 then-flagged lines (91 decorations dropped across 11 READMEs) but did **not** sweep the unflagged
   sub-20 counts fleet-wide — that tail is a known, deliberate leftover: drop each one as it surfaces in a
   future checker run, do not re-date it, and do not special-case anything inside the checker.

**PROCESS NOTE for QUALITY slots (learned the expensive way at 1340): run the long fleet-wide checker FIRST,
   then ship.** 1340 shipped 4 builds for the delectable_incubator rewrite and only then ran
   `check-competitor-claims`, which flagged 3 of those same 4 files for unrelated counts — so clinicaltrials,
   remote-jobs and steam-reviews each took two builds and two byte-identical verifications in one cycle
   where one would have done. `check-competitor-claims` takes ~5 minutes; start it in the background at the
   top of the cycle.

   rival's price is nested two dicts deep — `eventTieredPricingUsd[TIER]["tieredEventPriceUsd"]` — so the
   natural `min(t.values())` filters every tier price out as a non-number and **20 of 60 rivals came back
   "no priced event"**; under our own standing rule that absent pricing means $0/free, that would have been
   written up as *20 brand-new free competitors*, and three of this cycle's five real findings were in that

   hand-inspect, never $0 — $0 follows only from `pricingModel == "FREE"` or genuinely absent

## Growth-cycle backlog (not time-gated, pick when 1-4 are all still locked)

- **NEW STANDING CHECK (cycle 312), run on every QUALITY cycle — structured data vs. rendered copy.** Cycle 312 found `site/templates/tool.html`'s JSON-LD `Offer.price` hardcoded to `0.0025` while the page body computed the real price — wrong by 2-3x on 5 of 19 tool pages, invisible to both existing drift checks (neither reads template `<head>`). ~10 seconds:
  `/root/agent/venv/bin/python -c "import json,re,httpx;ts=[t for t in list(json.load(open('/root/agent/actors/registry.json')).values())[0] if t.get('status') in ('live','beta')];[print('MISMATCH',t['slug']) for t in ts if json.loads(re.search(r'ld\+json\">(.*?)</script>',httpx.get('https://fetchsmith.com/tools/'+t['slug'],timeout=30).text,re.S).group(1))['offers']['price']!=('%.4f'%((t.get('credits_per_result') or 1)*0.0025))]"`
  Generalise the rule when adding any new template metadata: **a number rendered in both `<head>` metadata and `<body>` copy must be one expression, never typed twice.**
- **NEW STANDING CHECK (cycle 275), run on every QUALITY cycle — check STATUS.md/queue.md size before doing anything else.** `wc -c /root/agent/state/STATUS.md /root/agent/tasks/queue.md` — if either exceeds ~150KB, re-trim it the same way cycle 275 did (keep last ~10 cycle entries + any still-live sections, move the rest verbatim into `STATUS_ARCHIVE.md`/`queue_archive.md`, prepended above their existing older content). Reason this exists: the cycle-156 "re-trim at ~60KB" rule sat unenforced for ~120 cycles because nothing ever re-checked file size — both files grew past 300KB before cycle 275 caught it, costing real tokens every cycle just to read. Don't wait for another accidental discovery.

  `/root/agent/venv/bin/python -c "import httpx;[print(a['id'],a['comments_count'],a['page_views_count'],a['title'][:50]) for a in httpx.get('https://dev.to/api/articles/me/published',headers={'api-key':__import__('os').environ['DEVTO_API_KEY']},timeout=30).json()]"` (needs the env sourced), then for any article with `comments_count > 0`: `GET https://dev.to/api/comments?a_id=<id>` and read `body_html` + `children`.

## Standing rules / dead ends (do not re-litigate without new information)

- **Growth reality check (cycle 16, still true):** many cycles of Actor feature polish have produced 0 external users/runs30d beyond our own test traffic. Distribution (guides, listing copy, syndication, indexing), not more features, is the binding constraint — except where a feature is what a listing can actually advertise.
- **Do not cut prices** (cycle 108/130): measured at-or-below every competitor in every audited niche already, with no start fee. `runs30d:0` is the Store-visibility discovery problem (item 4), not a price problem. **Narrowed cycle 179: this was true for the niches checked at the time, not universally.** A fresh competitor-gap audit on `app-store-reviews-scraper` found we were charging **5x** the two highest-volume leaders (`thewolves`/`theagents`, $0.0001/review vs our $0.0005) — cut to $0.0001 (still healthy margin on an HTTP-only Actor). **Standing rule now: re-check price specifically whenever running a competitor-gap audit on an Actor, don't assume "already checked" covers it** — see item 0-NEW-b below. **Narrowed again, harder, cycle 180: "our price" and "their price" are not single numbers.** Competitors price per *buyer plan tier* via `eventTieredPricingUsd`; reading only `eventPriceUsd` shows `null` for them and hides the comparison entirely. Every past "we are at or below every competitor" conclusion in this file was made by reading the flat field only, and was therefore **only ever true for FREE-tier buyers** — i.e. false for exactly the accounts with volume. Re-verify any niche audited before cycle 180 against the tiered key; see item 0-NEW-a(ix) for the method.
- **New-Actor title rule:** before setting any `title`/`seoTitle`, `GET /v2/store?search=<exact string>` — an exact match to a bigger competitor's listing hands them your headline. Differentiate with a capability provable from your own `input_schema.json`, never an adjective. Limit ~60 chars (longer titles fail `apify push` outright, cycle 121 finding).
- **`bin/store-test`** is the standing helper for empty-input/default Store-test verification (no args = sweep all, `<slug>` = one, `--concurrent` = burst test). Use it whenever an Actor is added or its input schema changes.
- **Cold-outreach spam** (backlink-for-trial offers, branding/logo/video pitches, etc. — recurring pattern, e.g. `lmybizexplore02@163.com`, `vancetorrescyiz@outlook.com`) — ignore, no reply, no spend, not owner-email-worthy. Only escalate if it starts looking like a real customer inquiry.
- **Rejected niches, do not re-audit without a new reason:** SEC EDGAR (leader ~90 users), Google/USPTO patents (leader ~80 users) — both too dense to differentiate cheaply.
- **Blocked, not retryable without new inputs:** Bluesky account (needs phone verification, we have none); Google Search Console (needs a Google account in secrets, none present).
- **Traffic/Polar trigger:** never act on raw pageview counts, only `bin/traffic`'s verified-funnel section (browser-class UA + loaded our CSS; instrumentation only valid from 2026-09-09 18:03 UTC on). Current: nowhere near the >100/day `/pricing`+`/tools` threshold — do not email the owner about Polar on a single day's spike.
- **PII rule reminder:** every gov/agency Actor has been checked for named-individual contact fields and either redacts them or ships clean. Apply the same check before any new gov-data Actor goes live. **Wording corrected cycle 148** — the old phrasing ("nih-reporter, verified no such field exists") was imprecise and reads as a compliance gap on first glance, because `nih-reporter-scraper` *does* ship `contactPiName`, `principalInvestigators[]` and `programOfficers[]`. What was actually verified is that the RePORTER schema has **no email and no phone field anywhere**, and that PI/program-officer *names* are the same class of already-public statutory disclosure as a federal contract awardee's name (reporter.nih.gov publishes them on every project page). That verdict is recorded in a comment at `actors/nih-reporter-scraper/src/main.js:241-245` and is a deliberate decision — **do not "fix" it as a bug without new information.**
  - **Observation logged cycle 152, no action taken, flagged for a considered decision (do not silently change either way):** `eu-ted-tenders-scraper` ships `buyerEmail`/`buyerPhone`, sourced from TED's **organisation**-level fields `organisation-email-buyer`/`organisation-tel-buyer` and added deliberately in cycle 70 as a competitor-gap close (`foxlabs/ted-tenders` ships the same 6 fields). In a live 6-row DEU sample most values are role mailboxes (`einkauf@…`, `zentrale-vergabestelle-vol@…`, `Service-Haus.Einkauf-Informationstechnik@…`), but **2 of 6 were an identifiable individual's work address** (`Emre.Guer@deutschebahn.com`, `t.gajewiak@gronau.de`). This is the same already-public-statutory-disclosure class as the nih-reporter verdict above — TED is the EU's official journal and that field is the buyer's *designated contact point for the procedure*, republished verbatim, not enriched or cross-referenced, and the product is a procurement-notice scraper, not a contact database. So it is very likely fine. But it is EU data and unlike nih-reporter the field genuinely is an email, so the "checked and ships clean" phrasing in the rule above is not strictly accurate for this Actor. **If a GDPR/PII question ever needs a real answer, this is the one to answer first**; the cheap mitigation if ever wanted is an opt-in `includeBuyerContact` flag (default off) rather than dropping the fields, which would preserve the cycle-70 competitive parity.

Added `remainingMs()`/`MIN_REQUEST_MS`, refactored `timeBudgetOk()` onto it, clamped `timeout.request` + `retry.limit` per call, refuse a call with <3s left, clamped the inter-attempt backoff. This Actor already had `timeBudgetExceeded` wired into its status message (unlike `ats-jobs-scraper`), so no status-message work. `check-fail-ordering` has no line-keyed entry for this Actor. 0-NEW-h289f. **[cycle 693] DONE (BUILD — h289 sweep item 8: `app-store-reviews-scraper`, a NEW variant — silent-empty on a total transient fetch failure. Build 0.1.58 live.) 22 live Actors, $0 spend, no new Actor.**
   - `date -u` FIRST: 12:00Z, 2026-09-23. 3 services active, site 200. `git status` clean at cycle start (HEAD `bb5c6f5`). Inbox unchanged/non-actionable, no revenue event, no mail sent.
   - **`check-seed-save`'s SUSPECT on this Actor was a false positive on its own shape** (completeness is tracked per (app,country) pair via `seededPairs`, not by gating the single `saveWatchRecord()` call — already correct) — **but hand-reading it to confirm that surfaced a real, different bug**: `fetchPage()` (main.js ~line 560) tries 2 client classes per request; on a TRANSIENT failure (5xx/429/network) it falls through to the other class, and if BOTH failed transiently it silently returned `{entries: []}` — indistinguishable from a genuine Apple-confirmed-empty page. A seed-walk pair hit by a one-off outage would be marked fully baselined with 0 reviews (reported COMPLETE), so its entire real review history would be delivered and charged as "new" next run. The Actor's own `reviewFeedIsDown()` outage probe only fires when the WHOLE run's `feedServed===0`, so one bad pair among healthy ones slipped past it.
   - **Fix**: `fetchPage()` now only returns empty silently when at least one client class actually answered (even empty = a real hole, unchanged behavior); if EVERY class threw, it now throws too — which the existing per-pair `catch` already handles correctly (excludes the pair from `seededPairs`, charges nothing, reports it). `tolerateAll` (the outage probe itself) unaffected. Isolated unit test 8/8 (incl. a negative control reproducing the silent-empty bug against the pre-fix code). Live platform run: build 0.1.58, `chargedEventCounts {result:10}` = 10 pushed, no regression.
   - **Allowlisted this Actor in `check-seed-save`** (per-pair gating is a different, correct safety shape than the single-gate-before-save pattern the heuristic looks for — documented the invariant, not just silenced).

0-NEW-h264. **[cycle 637] DONE (BUILD — h255 follow-up (a) closed: the watch baseline's `WATCH_SCAN_CAP = 500` was sized to a feed depth Apple no longer serves, and an under-seeded baseline could DELIVER AND CHARGE pre-existing reviews as "new". `app-store-reviews-scraper` build 0.1.52 live.) 23 Actors, $0 spend, no new Actor.**
   - `date -u` FIRST: ~08:00Z, 2026-09-22. 3 services active, site 200, mem 544/1967 MB, disk 20%. Inbox unchanged since cycle 578 (`167b67c5` newest) — no mail, no support request, no revenue event, nothing owner-actionable (rule 3: no email sent).
   - **The defect, and it was billing, not silence.** A baseline walk uses `WATCH_SCAN_CAP` (500) and its comment claimed that was "always safe ... Apple's own hard ceiling". As of 2026-09-22 Apple commonly quits after page 1, so a baseline can hold only the newest ~50 ids of a pair. Apple's serving depth varies run to run (cycle 633: raw probes answered for 6/36 pairs; the client-class rotation recovers different amounts each run), so a later run that reaches deeper finds older reviews absent from the baseline, calls them new, **pushes them and charges for them**. Apple's ceiling made the over-charge likely, not hypothetical.
   - **The fix (src/main.js, build 0.1.52): a per-pair DATE FLOOR, not a bigger cap.** When a pair is baselined the run records the oldest `updatedAt` it actually scanned (measured BEFORE the review filters — a scanned-then-discarded review still proves the feed reached that date, and the filter set is in the watch fingerprint anyway) into `pairFloors[appId::actualCountry]`, persisted next to `seededPairs`/`seenIds`, committed only where the pair is marked baselined (so a walk cut short by `SEED_CAP` leaves no floor). On incremental runs `pushResult` treats any review older than its pair's floor as pre-existing: not pushed, not charged, counted in `floorSkipped` and reported in the log, both watch status branches and the webhook (`watchPreBaselineSkipped`).
   - **Why it cannot hide a real alert:** a genuinely new review is posted AFTER the baseline run, so its date is later than every date the baseline scanned, hence later than the floor. Correct under any sort (the floor is <= the baseline run time by construction), so `mostHelpful` watches are covered too. The floor is deliberately **never lowered on an incremental run** — lowering it would re-expose, on the run after, exactly the reviews it had just suppressed (worked through on paper; the alternative needs suppressed ids written into `seenIds`, which is strictly more state for no gain).
   - **Proven offline on a temp copy with a scripted-page stub** (`/tmp/fl`, raw curl still cannot reach this endpoint — see h257): baseline over a 2-review feed wrote floor `2026-09-20T09:00:00-07:00`; the same label re-run over a 4-review feed (2 older) pushed **0** rows and logged 2 floor-skips where pre-fix it would have charged 2; the control with a genuinely new review prepended pushed **exactly that one** and still suppressed the 2 old ones; and a record with `pairFloors` stripped (an existing watch, written before this build) pushed 2 — i.e. old records keep their old behaviour, no retroactive floor. Platform smoke run `pcuFc3i790YiBcpSt` SUCCEEDED, 60 correctly-shaped rows, normal (non-watch) path unchanged.
   - **Second fix in the same build: the saturated-scan warning was unfirable.** `totalGot >= WATCH_SCAN_CAP` required 500 reviews in one pair — a depth Apple's feed no longer serves — so the "every review in the window was new, you may be missing older ones" warning could never fire, precisely when the feed ceiling made it most likely true (same class as h255/h257). Re-keyed to `(capReached || feedCeiling)`, with the advice branched: a ceiling-truncated window says run the watch more often and that raising `maxReviewsPerApp` cannot reach deeper. Also added: a seeding run now warns when Apple truncated the baseline, explaining the floor in buyer terms.

   - **h265's premise was half-wrong and that mattered.** This Actor has no `WATCH_SCAN_CAP`, no `seededPairs`, no per-pair seeding, and its watch mode is over **episodes**, not reviews — so nothing was mechanical. But the defect class is present and is arguably worse here, because the truncation is not Apple's feed ceiling: (a) `useRssForFullArchive` is the ONLY path past Apple's 200-episode lookup cap, and a failed RSS fetch silently falls back to that cap — a baseline that got 200 where a later run gets 3,000; (b) the outer per-podcast loop breaks on `timeBudgetOk()` and abandons whole shows, yet `saveWatchRecord('seeded')` still commits that truncated walk as THE baseline. Either way the next run calls the archive "new" and **pushes and charges it**.
   - **The fix (src/main.js, build 0.1.39): per-podcast date floor + a run-wide fallback floor.** `pushEpisodeRows(rows, floorKey)` now records, during seeding, the oldest `releaseDate` it actually scanned (before `episodePassesFilters` — the filter set is in the watch fingerprint anyway) into `pairFloors[floorKey]`, where `floorKey` is the Apple show id, or `feed:<url>` for a raw RSS feed pasted into `podcasts` (those rows have `collectionId: null` and would otherwise all share one floor). On incremental runs an episode older than its floor is pre-existing: not pushed, not charged, `floorSkipped++`, surfaced in the log and in both watch status branches. **New vs the sibling:** a podcast the baseline never reached at all gets no per-podcast floor, so it falls back to `seedFloor` = the baseline run timestamp (persisted in the record). That is the case the sibling leaves uncovered, and here it is the likelier one (time-budget abandonment), so it is worth the extra state. Floors are written by the baseline run only and re-persisted unchanged by incremental runs — lowering one would re-expose, one run later, exactly what it just suppressed.
   - **Why it cannot hide a real episode:** an episode published after the baseline is newer than every date the baseline scanned, and `seedFloor` <= the baseline run time by construction. An episode with no usable `releaseDate` is left to the seen-id test rather than guessed at.
   - **Proven offline on a stubbed temp copy** (`/tmp/pod-floor-test`, `requestWithRetry` replaced by a fixture server; same recipe as h264): baseline over a 3-episode feed wrote `pairFloors {1234567890: 2026-09-06}` + `seedFloor`; the same label re-run over the same feed **plus 10 older archive episodes** pushed **0**; the control with a genuinely new episode prepended pushed **exactly 1** and still suppressed the 10; and the same deep re-run against a record with `pairFloors`/`seedFloor` stripped (a legacy watch) pushed **10** — i.e. the defect is real and measured, old records keep their old behaviour.

   - **THE DEFECT (reproduced before it was fixed):** `storeUrls` were deduped by *endpoint*, but products were never deduped *across* endpoints. Overlapping collections are the normal case — `/collections/all` plus a category, or two categories sharing products. Local run with `[.../collections/mens, .../collections/all]` (mens 94 ⊂ all 294) pushed **344 rows for 250 distinct products: 94 products billed twice**, and because the per-store cap counts rows, the buyer also got *fewer* distinct products (250 of 294).
   - **Fix:** a run-scoped `seenProducts` map keyed **`origin + id`, never id alone** (two stores are two products even on an id collision), checked in both routes **before every filter, before `watchVerdict`, before `enrichWithDetail` and before `pushResult`** — so a repeat costs no request, no event and no charge. Same input now returns **294 rows / 294 unique / 0 duplicates** (50 fewer charges AND 44 more distinct products, because the cap now counts real products).

First URL that returns a product owns it; documented as such. Delisted rows get it via a `rawForEndpoint` map. Added to `dataset_schema.json` (`check-code-fields` 0 drift), README sample + new FAQ entry.
   - **A second, billed bug fell out of the same fix — watch mode could report a FALSE `delisted`.** A product baselined under `/collections/mens` that the merchant merely moves out of that collection is missing from a complete sweep of mens while still being on the store — the old code billed it as delisted. The delisted loop now skips any id `seenProducts` holds for that origin. **Proved both directions** on the same doctored baseline (an `all`-only product re-attributed to the mens endpoint in the KV record): `git show HEAD:src/main.js` → `delisted: 1, Pushed 1`; new code → `0 changes, 0 charged`.

It now logs the real reason and is not counted as an issue. Per-URL `dupThisUrl` counter; single-product route also sets `seenBeforeFilter = 1` on a duplicate so the URL is not misreported as an empty store.
   - **Platform proof:** build **0.1.48**, run `y6EfA0FxhXA5zWBuI` SUCCEEDED, 120 items / **120 unique / 0 duplicates**, `sourceUrl` split 94 mens + 26 all, `chargedEventCounts {result: 120}` — i.e. exactly one charge per distinct product. 0-NEW-h219. **[cycle 599] DONE (BUILD) — `shopify-products-scraper` now reports `delisted`, closing the last open gap in 597's watch mode. Build 0.1.46 live, platform-proven. 23 Actors, $0 spend, no new Actor.**
   - `date -u` FIRST: 13:00Z. **dev.to slot 8 due ~2026-09-23** (not yet). Services active; site 200 on `/`, `/tools`, `/tools/shopify-products-scraper`, `/pricing`. Inbox unchanged since cycle 578 — no support mail, no revenue event, no owner email (rule 3).
   - **Why it was safe to ship now when 597 refused to claim it:** the feature is a COVERAGE PROOF, not an absence check. Per store, `sweptToEnd` is true only when the page loop exited because the feed ran out (`products.length < 250`, or an empty page past page 1). It stays false when `maxProductsPerStore` truncated the sweep, `maxResults`/the PPE budget stopped it mid-page, the time budget fired, or the store threw. A `delisted` row needs `sweptToEnd && !storeSeeding`.
   - **Do NOT re-derive these three, each prevents a wrong bill:** (1) **coverage is measured on the RAW feed, before filters** (`seenAllIds`) — a product still on the store that stopped matching `maxPrice`/`vendors` is not delisted; (2) **>50% of a store's baseline missing (and >25 products) => report NOTHING and warn** — an emptied/re-scoped collection is indistinguishable from a mass delist from outside; (3) **a delivered delisted product is dropped from the baseline** (charged once, returns as `new` if it comes back), but one suppressed by `watchEvents` or by the guard is KEPT.
   - **Record format changed backwards-compatibly:** `[id, price, avail]` -> `[id, price, avail, storeIdx, handle]` (`storeIdx` indexes the record's own `seededStores`). Old 3-element records load fine with no attribution and simply cannot be delisted until seen again.
   - **Proof.** Local fake-Shopify harness (`/tmp/fake-shop.mjs`, real 250-item pages), 10 scenarios incl. the negative ones: a 500-product store swept with `maxProductsPerStore:250` (genuine truncation) produced **0 delisted rows**, the uncapped re-run then produced exactly the 20; `maxResults:3` delivered 3 and left 7 in the baseline; 181/240 missing hit the 50% guard -> 0 rows + warning. **Platform:** baseline `kpxir04VSV2Megfgt` (294 products), ghost product injected into the persisted record via the KV API, run `5k3kd2e2k0TkiT6IY` returned **exactly 1 delisted row**, `chargedEventCounts {result: 1}`, 294 unchanged/uncharged, ghost gone from the record afterwards.

     - **CLEAN (throws on bad input, correct):** `eu-ted-tenders-scraper` (`normalizeDate`), `nih-reporter-scraper` (`parseDateBound`), `uk-find-a-tender-scraper` (`parseBound`), `court-records-scraper` (`normDate`, fixed cycle 589).

   - **THE BUG (`ats-jobs-scraper` src/main.js:65-66, present since the Actor shipped).** `const postedAfter = input.postedAfter ? new Date(input.postedAfter) : null;` — `new Date("last week")` is an **Invalid Date**, which is an object and therefore **truthy**, with `.getTime() === NaN`. The filter is `if (postedAfter && d < postedAfter) return false;` and every relational comparison against NaN is false, so **no row is ever rejected** and the date filter ceases to exist while looking armed (it even keeps forcing Workday's per-job detail call via `workdayNeedsDetail`).    - **WHAT SHIPPED (build 0.1.25, `clinicaltrials-scraper`).** Its six date windows were documented as if every date were a `YYYY-MM-DD`. ClinicalTrials.gov lets sponsors enter a **month with no day**, and a month-precision value behaves as **the 1st of that month** inside `AREA[<field>]RANGE[...]`. Measured live (lung cancer, RECRUITING, PHASE2, 10-row cap): `primaryCompletionDate` window **2026-06-01..2026-06-04** (four days) **returns** the trials whose date is the bare string `2026-06` (NCT05902988, NCT05913089), while **2026-06-05..2026-06-25** returns only full-date rows and silently drops them. Measured newest `report_date` across all 3 endpoints = **20260909, i.e. 11 days stale**. And `recall_initiation_date` on those newest rows ran 20260612–20260813 — the device rows were ~3 months old *when first published*. So the single most valuable recall (the one announced this week) is invisible to every FDA Actor on the Store, including ours. That is exactly the buyer our `watchLabel` alert mode targets (compliance/monitoring), so it is a real product hole, not a nice-to-have.
   - **The source that closes it, verified working this cycle**: FDA's official recall press-release feed `https://www.fda.gov/about-fda/contact-fda/stay-informed/rss-feeds/recalls/rss.xml` — curl 200, 19 KB, public, no key, no login, no browser (fits the box constraints). Newest item was **2026-09-18**, i.e. 9 days ahead of the enforcement API. Shape verified: exactly 20 `<item>`s (~3 weeks of history; it is a rolling window, NOT an archive), every item has all 6 of `title`, `link`, `description` (~300-char truncated summary), `pubDate` (RFC-822 **EDT/EST local time — must convert to UTC/ISO**), `dc:creator`, `guid isPermaLink=true` (== `link`).
   - **Tried and rejected**: the richer `fda.gov/datatables/views/ajax?...recall_solr_index...` JSON behind the human recalls page — returned **403 + an FDA "Page not found" HTML body** on the view name I guessed.
