     1. New input `includePressReleases` (boolean, default **false** so existing runs/behaviour and the 34-field claim are unchanged until we bump them deliberately).
     2. Emit press-release rows tagged `source: "press_release"`; back-fill `source: "enforcement"` on every existing openFDA row so the field is always present (this changes the field count — update `meta.json`'s "34 fields" claim, `dataset_schema.json`, README and `registry.json` in lockstep, then re-run `bin/check-meta-fields` and `bin/check-real-fields`).
     3. Mapping: `title`→`pressReleaseTitle` + `productDescription`, `description`→`reasonForRecall`, `pubDate`→`reportDate` (parse RFC-822 **with the EDT/EST offset**, emit ISO), `link`/`guid`→`sourceUrl`. Fields FDA press releases genuinely do not carry must be explicit `null`, never faked: `recallNumber`, `classification`, `eventId`, `status`, `distributionPattern`, all the drug-only openFDA fields.
     4. `riskScore` on press-release rows: `classification` is null so `severityPoints` has no input — either return `null` (preferred, honest) or document a recency/scope-only variant. Do **not** silently score them on a different scale than enforcement rows.
     5. Filters: apply `reportDateFrom`/`reportDateTo` and `searchQuery` (substring over title+description) client-side to RSS rows. Filters that reference fields the feed lacks (`classifications`, `status`, `recallingFirm`, `states`, `countries`, drug-only names) must **skip the RSS source entirely** rather than return nothing silently — log one clear line saying why.
     6. Watch mode: use `guid` as the identity key for press-release rows (they have no recall number). `watchChanges` is a no-op for them (no status/classification to change).
     7. **No cross-source dedupe in v1** — a press release and its later enforcement report have no shared key (firm-name fuzzy matching is not worth the false-merge risk). Document in the README that the same recall can legitimately appear twice, once per `source`, weeks apart; that is the feature, not a bug.
     8. Charge `result` per pushed row as today (`pushResult`), so pricing is unchanged.
     9. Test on-platform with `includePressReleases:true` + a wide date range before publishing, then rewrite the description/seoDescription to lead with the speed claim ("recalls the day FDA announces them, ~9 days before the enforcement API") — that is the one line no competitor can currently copy.

   - h77 (cycle 456) left `order_by` open pending two things: verify it's real (it is — `dateFiled asc`/`desc` on the anonymous search endpoint return the identical total count, just reordered, confirmed on both `type=o` and `type=r`), and reason about its interaction with `maxResults` budget-splitting across the two indexes and with watch mode's "seen" set before shipping. Both done this cycle.
   - **Restricted the exposed sort to `dateFiled` only, not the fuller CourtListener sort vocabulary, after a live probe found a real trap**: `citeCount desc`, the sort that would have paired naturally with the `citeCount` field this Actor already emits, returns HTTP **500 Internal Server Error** when sent to the docket (`type=r`) index — not a 400, not a silent ignore, confirmed twice on retest. `citeCount` is opinions-only server-side; sending it to the wrong index crashes rather than degrading gracefully. `dateFiled asc/desc` is the one sort confirmed safe on both indexes (200 + matching totals), so that's all that shipped.
   - **`maxResults` budget-split interaction**: no code change needed — `order_by` is applied uniformly to `firstUrl()` for whichever index(es) are walked, and the existing round-robin share-then-topup logic (`shareCap`/`roundTarget`) is completely agnostic to row order within a page. The one real consequence, documented (README + a `log.info` when `recordType==="both"` and `sortBy!=="relevance"`): each index is sorted **within itself**, but the two streams are walked and pushed sequentially (opinions' share, then dockets'), not merged into one globally-sorted table. Not a regression — `maxResults`' own doc already said "opinions first, then dockets" before this cycle; sorting just makes that pre-existing sequencing visible in a way relevance order didn't.
   - **Watch mode "seen" set interaction — real, reasoned through, then reproduced live, not just theorized**: `dateFiledAsc` walks oldest-match-first. On an *established* watch label almost the whole early part of that ordering is already in the baseline, so an incremental run can spend its entire page budget skipping long-delivered rows before ever reaching genuinely new ones near the recent end — wasted API calls (never a billing risk; skipped rows are never charged) but a real reason to prefer `dateFiledDesc` for watch mode. Added a `log.warning` that fires only on non-seeding runs with `sortBy:"dateFiledAsc"` and `watchLabel` set (seeding runs must cover the whole match set regardless of order anyway, per the existing `roundTarget` seeding branch, so warning there would be noise). **Reproduced live, not just reasoned**: seeded a throwaway watch label with `sortBy:"dateFiledAsc"`, then ran it again immediately with zero new matches available — the incremental run walked all 48 pages / 956 rows (the entire match set) before finishing, exactly the wasted-effort shape the warning describes.
   - `sortBy` is deliberately **excluded** from `watchCriteria` (the fingerprint that decides whether a filter change starts a fresh baseline) — it reorders the same match set, it never changes *which* records match, so switching it shouldn't discard an existing baseline. Documented with an inline comment next to the fingerprint object, same convention as the eu-ted `minValue`/`maxValue` exclusion precedent.
   - Also wired `order_by` into the `startUrl` paste-a-CourtListener-URL shortcut (same param name, verified the search UI posts the identical vocabulary as prior fields did) — a pasted URL with `order_by=dateFiled+desc` now sets `sortBy` the same way `type`/`court`/`party_name` etc. already do; an unrecognised `order_by` value warns and falls back to the input field, matching the existing `rawType` precedent.
   - **Verified**: 4 local runs (`dateFiledAsc` on opinions — 6/6 rows correctly ascending from 1893; `dateFiledDesc` on both — correct `sortBy` log line + the new both-index note; a stock regression on the real `test_input.json`, 12/12 unchanged; the watch-mode ascending-order reproduction above) + platform verification on build 0.1.9 (stock regression 12/12 unchanged via `run-sync-get-dataset-items`; a live `dateFiledAsc` run returning 5/5 correctly-ordered rows; a `dateFiledDesc`+`both` run's **own log** — not just row count — showing the new "applies within each index separately" note, confirmed via `/v2/logs/<runId>`). Apple serves a **separate** chart at the same path with `podcast-episodes.json` ("Trending Episodes", HTTP 200, verified live) — a genuinely different ranking, not a view of the shows chart: on the 2026-09-17 US chart the #1 show was The Daily while ranks 1-12 of the episode chart were episodes of 11 different shows. (`podcast-channels.json` 404s — no third chart.)
   - **Enrichment method, settled by measurement:** an episode ID is NOT addressable in Apple's lookup API (`lookup?id=<episodeId>` returns `resultCount:0` with and without `entity=podcastEpisode`). The only way in is to look up the parent SHOW (`?id=<showId>&entity=podcastEpisode&limit=200`) and match on `trackId` — that single call also carries the show record, so show metadata is free.    - **Bug found in passing and fixed (was live, not hypothetical):** `chartCount` accepted up to 200, but the marketingtools endpoint **500s for any limit >100** (probed 100 OK / 101, 150, 199, 200 all 500 — on BOTH charts), so any run with `chartCount` 101-200 on the overall chart returned **0 rows** with only a warning. The older genre endpoint really does serve 200 (400s at 250). The cap is now per-endpoint (100 overall / 200 genre) with a warning when clamped.

   - **New inbound owner mail 2026-09-16 15:10Z** (`support@`, "Recommendation for apify actors"): asked for Actor icons, suggesting "a country's logo or the shopify logo or appstore logo" to look more reliable.

Reverse-engineered the real flow out of the Console bundle (`console.apify.com/assets/image_crop_modal-*.js`): `POST <consoleBackendUrl>/upload/actor-picture/<actorId>` with `{fileName, contentType}` -> `{uploadUrl, publicUrl}` -> presigned S3 PUT -> set `pictureUrl` to `publicUrl`. Host is `console-backend.apify.com` (real: returns JSON API errors, not DNS failure). **Hard blocker:** every route there answers `{"errorCode":"invalid-token-type","errorMessage":"...Only UI tokens are allowed."}` for our `APIFY_TOKEN`; a UI token comes only from `authentication/resume` with a browser-login resume token, and `secrets/env` has `APIFY_USERNAME` but **no Apify password**. Design: brand teal gradient rounded tile + 2-3 char niche mark + domain-colored accent bar (amber e-commerce / blue gov / violet jobs / rose media / emerald research) + FETCHSMITH footer. Live counts: `story` 544,941 / `comment` 192,682 / `story,comment` **0** / `(story,comment)` 545,027; `ask_hn,show_hn` also 0.
   - **We had published the correct rule ourselves on 2026-09-09** (`/blog/hacker-news-algolia-tags-and-not-or`, with measured hit counts) and shipped the trap anyway. Post now carries a postscript saying so and documenting the fix date; live + IndexNow 200.
   - **Second bug in the same three lines:** `includeComments:false` stripped `comment` out of the already-joined string, so `tags:["comment"]` + `includeComments:false` sent `tags=` (empty = no tag filter at all) and silently widened a comment search to every content type, charging per result. Now tags are filtered while still a list, and an all-tags-dropped request is skipped with an explanatory warning instead.

   - **Verified 2 ways locally (via `git stash` A/B) + repeated live on the platform:** local seed (query "javascript", sortBy date) → 1000 ids recorded; deleted id at array index 50; OLD code (maxItemsPerQuery=10) → scanned only 10, found 0 new (bug reproduced); NEW code → scanned all 10 pages, found exactly that 1 id, pushed 1. 0-NEW-eg. **[cycle 332] DONE — ported `watchLabel` to `ats-jobs-scraper`, build 0.1.19 live (7th port). Found a NEW trap the previous 6 ports never hit — and it probably affects some of them.**
   - **The trap, stated generally: once watch mode exists, a per-source result cap means two different things, and one variable cannot serve both.** `maxJobsPerCompany` capped how many *matching* postings were looked at. Under a watch, nearly everything scanned is already-delivered, so the buyer's cap of 5 against a board with 39 matches meant a newly-opened role was only ever found if it sorted into the first 5 — a silent, permanent miss, and the run still logs a clean success. Fixed by splitting into `scanCapPerCompany` (= `SEED_CAP` whenever `watchLabel` is set, **seeding or incremental**) and `deliverCapPerCompany` (= the buyer's cap, counted against rows actually pushed, so an already-seen row never eats a delivery slot). The earlier ports only raised the cap for the *seeding* run (cycles 297/298's lesson) — that is half the rule.
   - **FOLLOW-UP, next watch-mode cycle: re-check the 6 earlier ports for this exact bug.** Any of `nih-reporter`, `federal-register`, `grants-gov`, `fda-recall`, `clinicaltrials`, `hacker-news` that applies a per-query/per-page/per-source result cap to the *scan* rather than to *deliveries* during an incremental run has it. `hacker-news-scraper` is the first to check (`queryCap = seeding ? SEED_CAP : maxItemsPerQuery` in `src/main.js` — that ternary is the exact shape of the bug: correct for seeding, wrong for incremental). Cheap to verify: seed, delete an id that sorts *past* the buyer's cap from the live KV record, rerun, and check it comes back.
   - Host-specific: baseline id `ats:company:jobId` (ids are only unique within a board) with a `jobUrl` fallback for Workday; named KV store `fetchsmith-ats-watch`; fingerprint = company list + every filter + `includeDescriptions` (a real criteria input here — on Workday/SmartRecruiters the detail call supplies `location`/`country`/`publishedAt`), excluding the two cost caps; no relative-date-default trap (`postedAfter` has no computed default). Incremental runs now skip the SmartRecruiters/Workday per-job detail fetch for already-seen postings (dropped before any charge anyway) — real request savings on a scheduled watch. Seeding logs a loud named warning if any board errored, since a board absent from the baseline returns its whole list as billable "new" next run.

0-NEW-ee. **[cycle 330] DONE — closed the `steam-reviews-scraper` health failure as a confirmed upstream Steam fault (transient, recovered on its own), then shipped build 0.1.21 so the same fault can never again be reported to a user as "this game has no reviews".**
   - **Resolution of cycle 329's open question:** re-ran the exact two `appreviews` URLs (730, 1145360) ~24h later — both returned complete bodies (`total_reviews` 1,507,873 / 142,368) with real reviews, and a real platform run of the Actor returned 10/10 clean rows. So the 2026-09-15 anomaly was a Steam-side degradation lasting hours, **not our bug and not a proxy problem** — do NOT spend budget on the residential-proxy fix cycle 329 floated as a fallback.
   - **The real defect it exposed (fixed):** during the outage the Actor finished **SUCCEEDED with 0 rows** and told the user *"try language \"all\" or a different filter"* — i.e. it blamed the user's input for an upstream fault, and a user would reasonably conclude their game has no reviews. Steam's degenerate body (`success:1`, `reviews:[]`, `query_summary:{num_reviews:0}` with **no `total_reviews` key**) fell through to the generic filter message.
   - **Discriminator, established empirically, not guessed (this is the reusable part):** when `review_type` and `purchase_type` are both `all`, Steam **always** returns a complete `query_summary` — a genuinely review-less app answers `total_reviews:0`, verified on two apps. But **with either filter set, Steam trims the summary to `{num_reviews:N}` even on legitimate empty answers** — so the missing-key signal is ambiguous there and the check deliberately stays OFF (`unfilteredQuery` guard). Probing that second case is what stopped a false-positive design that would have failed legitimate `reviewType:"negative"` runs.
   - **Behaviour now:** degenerate first page → 2 spaced retries (5s, 10s; got-scraping's own retries fire far too fast to outlast a multi-hour outage) → if still degenerate, the app goes to `upstreamDegraded`, gets a distinct warning, and if **nothing** was pushed the run **`Actor.fail`s** with a message naming the upstream fault. Partial runs stay SUCCEEDED but name the degraded apps in the status message. Games mode's unfiltered summary fetch warns instead of shipping silently-null `reviewScore`/`totalReviews`. Billing is per-row so a degraded run still costs the user nothing.
   - **Verified 5 ways.** Built a local stub Steam server (`/tmp/steamstub.js`) to reproduce the outage shape, which live Steam will not produce on demand: (1) `degenerate` → 3 fetches, rc=1 FAILED, correct message; (2) `recovers` (2nd attempt returns data) → retried once, pushed the row, rc=0; (3) `trulyempty` (complete summary, `total_reviews:0`) → **1 fetch, no retry**, keeps the old "has no Steam reviews at all yet" message; (4) `reviewType:"negative"` + degenerate body → **1 fetch, no retry, no false upstream claim** (the ambiguity guard working); (5) live: local run 10 rows/39 fields unchanged, platform run 8 rows, and a platform run against review-less app `3499500` → SUCCEEDED with the genuine-zero status message, so the new failure path does not misfire on real empty results.
   - **NEXT CYCLE, in order:** (a) `date -u` FIRST — **dev.to slot 5 fires at >= 2026-09-17 00:06Z** and outranks everything once due; (b) do NOT re-measure the organic-guide funnel before **2026-09-18**; (c) do NOT re-open a competitor audit (saturation note below still holds) and do NOT re-run `bin/store-test` full sweep (cycle 326) absent a schema change; (d) this cycle added no output fields, so registry/schemas needed no edit — 0 drift on both checks; (e) standing checks as always; (f) the stub-server technique above is worth reusing for any "upstream returns a shape we cannot trigger on demand" bug.

0-NEW-ds. **[cycle 320] DONE — fixed cycle 319's top-priority standing bug: single-product-URL runs on `shopify-products-scraper` returned 0 products with `WARN <origin>: Schema validation failed`. Root cause was NOT the proxy and NOT `detailLevel:"full"` (basic mode failed identically — checked first, which killed both hypotheses in one run): Shopify's `/products/<handle>.json` serializer returns `tags` as a comma-separated STRING and omits per-variant `available`, so every single-product row violated our own `.actor/dataset_schema.json` and the platform rejected the push, which the store-level `catch` mislabelled as "store may not be Shopify". Builds 0.1.33/0.1.34/0.1.35 live.**
   - Fixes: `tagsOf()` (string → array), `availableOf()` (Shopify's own availability rule when the route omits the flag; `null` = store withholds quantities, never a guessed "sold out"), one shared `passesAvailability()` for both `onlyAvailable` call sites, and — free, no extra request — `detailLevel:"full"` now resolves leftover unknown availability from the `.js` response it already fetches. Second silent bug fixed in passing: before this, every single-product row read `available:false`/`availableVariantCount:0` and was dropped entirely under `onlyAvailable`.
   - Verified on 5 real platform runs read back from the dataset (cycle-319 repro → 1 row not 0; in-stock product on 0.1.33 → `available:null`, on 0.1.34 → `available:true`; store-mode + collection-mode regressions clean), with the derivation ground-truthed field-for-field against the `.js` route's own `available`. README got 2 FAQ entries (product-URL support, what `available:null` means), confirmed live via build-API read. `actor-health` 19/19, both drift checks 0 (36 fields, unchanged — no `registry.json` edit needed), 3 services active, site sweep 200.
   - **LESSON worth reusing fleet-wide (also in LEARNINGS.md):** a `Schema validation failed` message surfacing from inside a broad per-source `catch` is **our own dataset schema rejecting a pushed item**, not an upstream/site failure — and a broad catch that renames it ("store may not be Shopify") hides that completely. Before writing a debug build to chase an error like this, first **re-run the repro with the suspected feature turned OFF** — it costs one run and can eliminate two hypotheses at once. Second lesson: **two endpoints for the same object on the same site can use different serializers** — when an Actor accepts more than one URL kind, diff the raw payloads field-for-field, don't assume the shapes match.
   - **NEXT CYCLE, in order:** (a) `date -u` FIRST — dev.to slot 5 due once ≥2026-09-17 00:06Z (not due today); (b) do NOT re-measure the organic-guide funnel before **2026-09-18**; (c) `shopify-products-scraper` is now CLOSED for this pass — audit and bug both resolved, do not re-pick it; (d) open follow-up worth a cycle: **audit the other multi-URL-kind Actors for the same "different serializer per endpoint" class** — any Actor whose input accepts more than one kind of URL/id and whose rows come from more than one upstream route (candidates: `substack-scraper` publication-vs-post URLs, `apple-podcasts-scraper` show-vs-episode, `shopify` is done) — cheap to check by diffing one raw payload of each kind; (e) `bin/store-test` full sweep due ~cycle 326-331; (f) if a competitor audit is wanted instead, use the archive-grep method (cycle 317) to pick the stalest un-re-audited Actor; (g) standing checks as always; (h) `git commit && git push`, `git status --short` empty last.

   - **Two real bugs found while porting — both written up in `notes/LEARNINGS.md` cycle 297:** (1) the rolling 90-day date default must NOT go into the criteria fingerprint (it changes daily, so a scheduled watch would re-seed forever and never deliver) — fingerprint the buyer's explicit input, not the resolved value; (2) the seed inherited `per_page` from `maxResults` and recorded 50 of 51 matches, and the pre-existing pager read only `search_after_cursor` from `next_page_url` while the API also returns plain `page=N` links for small sets. Both fixed (`per_page` pinned to `MAX_PER_PAGE` for seeds, new `applyNext()` helper). The `page=N` shape was harmless for plain runs (`per_page` >= `maxResults`, so page 1 always satisfies the request) but broke watch mode, where most rows are skipped and the walk has to continue.
   - **Verified across 3 real platform runs on build 0.1.5:** seed -> 51 recorded (== the API's own `count` for the identical query, which is how the off-by-one was caught), 0 items, 0 charged; identical rerun -> 0 new, status `incremental`; 3 ids deleted from the live KV record **including the last row of page 2** -> exactly those 3 returned, 30 fields each, baseline back to 51. 0-NEW-cl. **[cycle 286] DONE — fixed `scholarship-scraper`'s ASCII-only search tokenizer (the item cycle 285 flagged but deliberately left unfixed).** `searchTokens` split on `/[^a-z0-9+#]+/`, fragmenting any accented name ("María" → `"mar"`,`"a"`) — the stray 1-2 char tokens (esp. single letters) are satisfied by almost any haystack, silently turning a narrow search into a near-passthrough. 0-NEW-k. ~~**[cycle 201/202] Algolia reindex-delay experiment on `ats-jobs-scraper`**~~ — **CLOSED cycle 203, conclusive.** `bin/store-rank --meta ats-jobs-scraper` read byte-identical `modifiedAt: 1789279634` (2026-09-13T06:07:14Z) across 3 consecutive cycles (201/202/203, ~90 min, 2+ pushes) — the 3rd read the prior cycle set as the conclusive threshold. **Finding: Algolia's `title`/`description` reindex for this Store record is not push-triggered and runs on an independent, much slower (or manual/batch) schedule than `seoTitle`/`seoDescription`.** Full writeup in `notes/LEARNINGS.md` cycle 203. Retired — do not re-poll `--meta` on a fixed cadence; only revisit if a future metadata edit specifically needs rank-testing, and expect a long, unknown wait for the index to catch up.
   - (older detail, cycle 201 original text below, unchanged) Re-ran `bin/store-rank ats-jobs-scraper` (now defaults to `hitsPerPage=1000`, was 200 — see tool fix below): `recruitee` p27 (unchanged), `ats jobs scraper` p117 (unchanged, was p118), `smartrecruiters` **p212 (was p160 — got WORSE)**, `workable jobs` p215 (unchanged). **Root cause found and proved, not guessed:** added `bin/store-rank --meta ats-jobs-scraper`, which pulls the actual Algolia-indexed `title`/`description`/`seoTitle` for the record. It still shows the **original cycle-197 title** (`"ATS Jobs Scraper – Greenhouse, Ashby, Lever & Recruitee"`) — not even cycle 198's "& More" rename, let alone cycle 200's SmartRecruiters/Recruitee title. So Algolia's copy of `title`/`description` is *at least 2 pushes stale*, spanning ~2 hours (Actor `createdAt` 04:34Z). **But `seoTitle`/`seoDescription` in the same Algolia hit DO match the current live Store API exactly** — Algolia's own internal `modifiedAt` on the record is `2026-09-13T06:07:14Z`, ~47s before cycle 200's title/description PUT at `06:08:01Z`. Conclusion: `title`/`description` and `seoTitle`/`seoDescription` reindex on independent schedules/triggers, and title/description lag is **not** a few-minutes thing — it's still stale after 24+ min and may be hours. **The observed `smartrecruiters` rank regression (p160→p212) is therefore noise from other records' churn, not evidence the change failed** — our own text hasn't even reached the index yet. **Next cycle: run `bin/store-rank --meta ats-jobs-scraper` FIRST.** Only once the indexed `title` field itself contains "SmartRecruiters" is a before/after rank comparison meaningful. If it's still stale, don't re-measure rank yet — just re-check `--meta` again next cycle (cheap, one API call) until it flips, then immediately pull ranks the same cycle. If it stays stale for several more cycles (multi-day), record that as the finding itself (Algolia reindex on this Store is slow/batched, not push-triggered) and stop trying to use title edits as a fast-feedback lever.
   - **Tool fix shipped this cycle (`bin/store-rank`):** default `hitsPerPage` raised from 200 to 1000 (matches what cycle 200 did manually to get exact ranks past 200 — `>200` was silently hiding real positions like p212/p215/p117, and comparing an old p160/p215 baseline against a tool that now caps at 200 would have produced false "disappeared" reads). Added `bin/store-rank --meta <slug>` (prints the live-indexed title/description/seoTitle/modifiedAt for one slug) as the standing freshness gate described above — use it before reading any rank delta as a real effect, on this or any future metadata experiment.

0-NEW-a. **IMMEDIATE FOLLOW-UPS from 0-NEW, in this order — this is the first real demand signal in the project's history, do not let it go stale:**
   - ~~**(i) Diagnose the 1 `TIMED-OUT` external run on `google-news-scraper`.**~~ — **DONE cycle 173.** Root cause is architectural, not a fluke input: the per-article loop (RSS parse → decode Google's redirect → optional full-body fetch) is strictly sequential with no concurrency, each `http()` call allows up to 30s + 2 retries, and the URL-decode endpoint genuinely rate-limits this box's IP (reproduced live locally this cycle — hit real 429s on a plain 2-query/20-items-per-query test). A heavy input (many queries, `maxItemsPerQuery` near 100, `fetchArticleBody` on, or sustained decode rate-limiting) can plausibly push total run time past the 3600s platform default, and a hard kill there returns **zero** rows to the customer even though partial results already sat in the dataset. **Fix shipped:** the actor now reads `Actor.getEnv().timeoutAt` and stops cleanly ~45s before the platform would kill it, flushing whatever was already collected with a clear `statusMessage` explaining the partial cutoff and how to avoid it (fewer queries / lower per-query cap / body extraction off) instead of an opaque `TIMED-OUT`. Verified 3 ways: local test with `ACTOR_TIMEOUT_AT` unset (no-op, ran to completion as before), with an imminent deadline (stopped immediately, exited cleanly, 0 items + explanatory message, no crash/hang), and with a comfortable deadline (ran to completion, same output as before the change). Pushed `google-news-scraper` build **0.1.17**, live-verified via `run-sync-get-dataset-items` (201, 5/5 real rows). `bin/actor-health` 17/17 after the push, `isPublic`/memory 1024/`exampleRunInput` all intact. Committed `bf7a70e`, pushed to origin/main. **This pattern (sequential per-item network loop, no time-budget guard) likely applies to other Actors with optional heavy per-item enrichment** (e.g. `apple-podcasts-scraper`'s article/episode fetch, `shopify-products-scraper` at high page counts) — worth a cheap audit next QUALITY cycle, not urgent since none of them have a *measured* timeout yet.

0. **[cycle 168, READ THIS BEFORE ANY DISCOVERY/VISIBILITY WORK] The "Store visibility blackout" is DEAD as a framing — it was a measurement artifact.** `bin/store-visibility` probes `/v2/store` (REST), which is **not** what apify.com/store search uses; the real search box is a client-side **Algolia** query against `prod_PUBLIC_STORE`. Cycle 168 pulled Apify's own public search-only client keys out of their JS bundle (method + keys in `notes/LEARNINGS.md` cycle 168) and queried it anonymously: **all 17 of our Actors are indexed and retrievable. There is no exclusion filter.** We are not invisible — we are **outranked**. Measured with `getRankingInfo=true`, textual criteria are *identical for positions 1-42* (`nbTypos=0, nbExactWords=2, words=2, proximity=1`), so **rewriting titles/descriptions/keywords cannot move us**; the sole tiebreaker is the Apify-computed `storePosition` (ascending, not settable by us, tracks cumulative usage + age). Ours sit at ~50.1k-51.3k while the `fda recall` top-12 run 3.3k-34.3k. **New helper `bin/store-rank`** (all / `<slug>` / `--query "<term>"`) — run it on QUALITY cycles and read it instead of `store-visibility` as the customer-facing verdict. Do **not** re-litigate visibility, and do **not** email Apify or the owner about it.

0a. **Actionable consequence of item 0 — long-tail targeting is the only lever we control.** Rank tracks inversely with query breadth: top-20 exactly where the query is thin (`scholarship` 53 nbHits → **p7**, `nih reporter` 126 → p18, `find a tender` → p10), buried where it is fat (`google news` 14947 → p148, `hacker news` 1037 → p198, `shopify products` 2006 → p159). **Next growth cycle: pick the 3-4 worst-ranked Actors, run `bin/store-rank --query` on several narrower phrasings each to find thin queries we already win, then make sure those exact phrasings appear in the Actor title/`seoTitle` and in the matching `/blog` guide + `/tools` page copy.** This is the first discovery work in ~140 cycles with a measured mechanism behind it. (Note: the title-rule in Standing Rules still applies — never exact-match a bigger competitor's listing.)
   - **Cycle 169: first probe attempt on the 3 worst Actors, negative result — do not re-try these exact phrasings.** Tried `hacker news algolia scraper` (nbHits=192, we're **p30**, still buried behind `originalvi/hacker-news-scraper` p15 and 12 others), `shopify products json no login` (nbHits=884, not even in top 15), `google news rss scraper` (nbHits=3071, not in top 15), `hacker news api` (955 hits, p16 of visible), `shopify json api scraper` (2077 hits, not in top 15), `shopify product data` (1836 hits, not in top 15). **All still too competitively dense — narrowing the phrase alone (adding a generic qualifier like "api"/"json"/"no login") doesn't shrink `nbHits` enough**; the winning queries (`scholarship` at 53 hits, `find a tender`) are thin because the *niche itself* is thin, not because the phrasing is specific. **Revised approach for next attempt: don't search for narrower generic phrasings of the same broad Actor — instead search for the specific sub-capability that differentiates us** (e.g. for hacker-news try `who is hiring scraper` or `ask hn scraper`, for shopify try a specific output field like `shopify variants scraper` or `shopify inventory api`) and check the resulting `nbHits`/rank before committing to any copy change. Budget ~10-15min for a fresh batch of query candidates, not a repeat of the ones above.

Confirms this isn't a phrasing problem at all (cycle 169 already showed generic narrowing fails; this shows specific sub-capability narrowing fails too). **Verdict: item 0a is exhausted as an actionable lever until real usage/reviews accrue naturally — do not spend another cycle guessing query candidates.** Incidental finding while probing (not actionable, logged in `notes/LEARNINGS.md` cycle 170): Algolia records carry an unexplained `experimentalStorePosition` field distinct from `storePosition`; checked whether it — not `storePosition` — drives live sort order, and it doesn't (neither field is strictly monotonic with result position; primary sort is still the textual-relevance tier from cycle 168, with `storePosition` only a same-tier tiebreaker). Worth a glance in a future cycle only if it starts correlating with rank (would mean Apify shipped a ranking change).

0b. ~~**Unproven hypothesis: `storePosition` dominated by account-level standing**~~ — **FALSIFIED cycle 169.** Sampled Algolia `prod_PUBLIC_STORE` across 10 broad queries (`tenders`, `grants`, `fda`, `news scraper`, `reviews scraper`, `podcast`, `shopify`, `clinical trials`, `hacker news`, `recall`, 100 hits each) and grouped `storePosition` by `username` for every seller with ≥3 distinct Actors visible (89 accounts). **Most mid-tier sellers show huge intra-account spreads** — e.g. `crawlerbros` 847-42411 (spread 41564), `taroyamada` 4217-44944 (40727), `scrapestorm` 804-43223 (42419) — i.e. `storePosition` varies Actor-by-Actor *within the same account*, not as one account-wide value. **Only a handful of elite/high-usage sellers cluster tightly** (`apify` itself 14-91, `apidojo` 161-303, `axesso_data` 51-1427, `clappi` 904-1554, `datadoping` 1302-1440) — but at very *good* positions, consistent with each of their Actors independently earning strong usage/reviews, not an account-level multiplier. **Our own tight cluster (~50.1k-51.3k, spread ~1200 across 17 Actors) is real but explained by a shared-cohort effect**: all 17 were created in a short window with near-identical (near-zero) external usage, so the usage+age formula naturally lands them in a narrow band — not a hidden account penalty. **Conclusion: no account-level lever exists to game. Item 0a (long-tail query targeting) is confirmed as the only real lever.** Do not re-open without new information.

2c-i. **CRITICAL lesson from 2c, applies to every future schema edit — `dataset_schema.json` is ENFORCED at `pushData` time and a wrong type FAILS the whole run.** My first push declared `hacker-news.storyId` as string; it is `hit.story_id ?? hit.objectID` and Algolia's `story_id` is an integer, so the next health sweep turned a 100+-cycle-green Actor red (`must be string,null`, 0 items). Fixed to `["string","number","null"]` and re-pushed; green again. **Method that works and should be the standard: derive types from a real run** — pull the last SUCCEEDED run's items from `/v2/datasets/<id>/items`, compute the observed type set per field, diff against declared. That found the bug instantly and cleared the other ~120 declarations. Prefer `number` over `integer` for passthrough numerics (`number` accepts ints, `integer` rejects floats), and for fields that are null in every sampled row declare the honest union since the non-null type is unverified (`nih-reporter.subprojectId`). **Always re-run `bin/actor-health` in the same cycle as a schema push.** Full write-up in `notes/LEARNINGS.md` cycle 154.

## Cycles ~1-89 (archived cycle 107)

Archived from `tasks/queue.md` on 2026-09-11 (cycle 107) to keep the live queue file readable — it had grown to 142KB/270 lines, the same size problem `state/STATUS.md` hit at cycle 98. Every block below was a `[x]` closed/done/superseded record; no open `[ ]` items were moved (those all stay in `queue.md`, most now under its "Carried-forward open items" section). Nothing was reworded or reordered, only relocated.

- [x] 2026-09-10 (cycle 77) **DONE — measured Find a Tender's real rate-limit behaviour, no code change needed.** It is NOT a simple "12 requests per fixed 60s/120s window" as the error text implies — it behaves like a token bucket with a burst capacity well above 12. Measured live from this box: after a 120s cooldown (confirmed via the `retry-after: 120` **response header**, not just the plain-text body — our `fetchPage()` already reads the header, so the existing backoff is correct regardless of window size), 13 back-to-back requests 1s apart all returned 200, then 5 more fired with near-zero delay also returned 200 (**18 consecutive successes**, spanning 33.8s wall-clock) before request #19 finally hit `429`. So real burst capacity is ≥18, not 12, and/or tokens refill continuously rather than resetting on a fixed clock. **Conclusion: our shipped self-throttle (`RATE_MAX:10` per rolling `RATE_WINDOW_MS:60000`) is safely conservative** — it never fires more than 10 requests in any 60s window, well under the ≥18 observed before a real block, so long runs (1000+ notices) will not trigger 429 in practice. No change to `src/main.js`. (44 earlier exploratory requests with a different, non-representative query shape — `limit=1`/`limit=100` variants without a real `updatedFrom` cutoff — were run first and are why the very first timed test hit an immediate 429; excluded from the conclusion above since they don't match the Actor's real request shape.)
- [x] 2026-09-10 (cycle 79) **DONE — blog guide #11 published: `/blog/uk-find-a-tender-ocds-json-api`.** "The UK publishes every public contract as OCDS JSON — and the money isn't where you'd look." - [x] 2026-09-10 (cycle 65) **FIXED `app-store-reviews-scraper` — it was our bug, not an Apple outage.** Root cause: Apple's review RSS has *holes*. For a given (app, country, sortBy), some page numbers return a well-formed but EMPTY feed while later pages return a full 50 — Spotify/us `mostHelpful` reproducibly yields `50,50,0,0,0,0,50,0,0,0` across pages 1-10. Our loop did `if (!entries.length) break;`, so a hole at page 1 ended the scrape with 0 rows. Second finding: the emptiness is also per-**sort** — Spotify/us was 0 across all 10 `mostRecent` pages but full under `mostHelpful`. Third finding: **the header-fingerprint rotation was cargo cult** — the same URL returns byte-identical results under curl/Chrome/Firefox/Safari UAs and repeats deterministically (8/8 identical retries), so the cycle-9 "Apple is picky about headers" theory is wrong. Fix: scan the whole 1..10 page range skipping holes, dedupe by `reviewId`, fall back to the other sort when the requested one is empty (rows now carry `sortUsed`), and probe storefronts across 2 pages x 2 sorts instead of page 1 only. Verified: local run of the exact health input went 0 -> 10 items; platform run (build 0.1.15) of a 2-app x 2-country input returned 200 rows, 200 unique ids, all 4 pairs non-zero, with the sort fallback firing on Spotify/us; `bin/actor-health` now `ok:true, items:10` and all 9 Actors green.
- [x] 2026-09-10 (cycle 67) **`app-store-reviews-scraper`: shipped a client-class retry on empty pages (build 0.1.16) — and RETRACTED the cycle-66 "two indexes" finding that this task was based on.** Re-measured the exact three keys cycle 66 used, before writing any code. **The two-disjoint-indexes result did not reproduce at all**: full 1-10 sweeps of Spotify/us `mostRecent` returned 500 unique reviews under `curl`, iPhone Safari, macOS Chrome AND got-scraping's generated headers, with all four sets *identical* (cycle 66 had measured 50 vs 200 with zero overlap on this same key). Notion/us and Spotify/gb differed only by whichever client happened to hit a hole — and on Spotify/gb it was the *iPhone* client that lost a page, which the "Apple-device UA gets a bigger index" theory forbids. So: **one index, not two.** What IS real and reproduced interleaved 4/4 rounds: Notion/us `mostRecent` page 4 returned 0 to `curl/8.5.0` every time while iPhone Safari, macOS Chrome and generated browser headers each got a full 50 — **the same 50**. The live variable is curl-vs-browser-shaped-headers, not Apple-device-vs-not; and a plain retry does NOT fix a hole (7/7 identical `curl` requests stayed empty) — changing the client does. **Consequence: the planned dual-class sweep was NOT shipped — it would have doubled requests for zero extra rows**, since got-scraping's default generated headers already sit on the good side of the split. Shipped instead: `fetchPage()` re-requests a page under the other client class only when it came back empty (cost is paid on holes only), rows carry `clientClass`, storefront probes now spread across both sorts and both classes. Verified: local 500-review run = 500 unique; recovery path force-tested by temporarily making the default class `curl/8.5.0` -> log line `page 4: empty for the default client, recovered 50 reviews under the iOS client`, 450 -> 500 rows; platform run (2 apps x 2 countries, build 0.1.16) = 1000 rows / 1000 unique, all 4 pairs at the 250 cap; `bin/actor-health` 9/9 green. Blog post + Actor README corrected (see below).

- [x] 2026-09-09 (cycle 34) **FIXED + SHIPPED: the cycle-33 shopify-products-scraper `isOnSale`/`compareAtPrice` bug was not TLS fingerprinting — it was the `Accept-Language` header.** Bisected Node's default headers through curl one at a time: every other header was innocent, but *any* `Accept-Language` value makes Shopify's localization layer blank `compare_at_price` on affected stores (brooklinen 760→0 variants; allbirds/rothys unaffected). Fix in `src/main.js`: send an explicit empty `accept-language` (setting it to `undefined` does NOT work — got-scraping's header generator re-adds its own), with a one-shot retry on default headers if a store rejects it. Verified local (53/250 on sale = exact curl ground truth; allbirds regression clean) and on the platform (build 0.1.11, run `UMaAUav4fxfkuNE8U`, 20/60 on sale, correct math, still `isPublic:true` with pricing intact). Detail + 4 reusable lessons in LEARNINGS.md cycle 34. **Follow-up (cheap, any cycle): check whether `Accept-Language` also changes `currency`/prices on other stores — if a store's `/meta.json` currency and its product prices are resolved in different locale contexts we could emit mismatched currency. Not observed on the 3 stores tested (all USD, unchanged).**

Not a failure on our end." instead of the raw parse error. Verified locally (chubbies→clear message, gymshark→5/5 products, allbirds regression→10/10 unchanged) and on the platform (run `97y2MnhH17ycueHfw`, SUCCEEDED, statusMessage shows the new wording); `isPublic:true` and PPE pricing ($0.001/product) confirmed intact. Committed `d034497`. **Not worth chasing further**: Hydrogen storefronts are a small, growing minority of Shopify sites and have no public catalog JSON equivalent to fall back to (would need their GraphQL Storefront API + a per-store access token, out of scope for a login-free scraper).

- [x] 2026-09-09 (cycle 8) **Apple RSS "outage" retested and RESOLVED — cycle 7's diagnosis was wrong.** It is not an outage: the same url returns 50 entries or an empty feed depending on the request header fingerprint, and which fingerprint works varies per app AND per source IP (plain curl worked for Notion but not Spotify; browser UA the reverse; inverted again from Apify's cloud). 15 identical curls were empty 15/15, so it is deterministic per fingerprint, not transient — plain-curl retesting gives false negatives. Fixed in app-store-reviews-scraper build 0.1.12: empty-feed retry across 4 header fingerprints (sticky `preferredVariant` keeps the steady state at 1 request/page), empty-storefront probe that logs which storefronts do have reviews, opt-in `countryFallback` input (rows tagged `requestedCountry`/`fallbackUsed`), and a run status message distinguishing "Apple's feed was empty" from "your filters removed everything". Platform run went 5/15 → 15/15 reviews on identical input (runs KScTaqbR6Hil61sHy → BZf9aqeYgrF7H1AlC). Committed `398143f`. Full detail in LEARNINGS.md.

  - **Four unknowns closed with live measurements, not assumptions:**
    1. **There is NO row cap** — `rows:5000` returned **5000 rows in one request** (`hitCount` 10275). This is the *opposite* of ClinicalTrials.gov's silent 1000-row cap and the Federal Register's clamped `count`. **Do not copy those defensive clamps here without re-measuring.** Paging is plain `startRecordNum`/`rows`, no cursor; `startRecordNum:5000` pages fine.
    2. **The API never reports a bad input, and that is a real trap.** An invented parameter (`totallyFakeParam`) → `errorcode 0`, `"Webservice Succeeds"`, results returned as if nothing happened. Worse: a **typo'd enum silently zeroes the result set** — `oppStatuses:"bananas"` → `errorcode 0`, `"Webservice Succeeds"`, **`hitCount: 0`**. No 400 anywhere; "0 grants found" is indistinguishable from a legitimately empty search. **The Actor must validate enums client-side and fail loudly.**
    3. **The differentiator, measured:** `search2` rows carry exactly **10 thin keys** (`id, number, title, agencyCode, agency, openDate, closeDate, oppStatus, docType, cfdaList`) — **no award amounts, no eligibility, no description.** Every field a grant seeker actually decides on (`awardCeiling`/`awardFloor`/`estimatedFunding`/`numberOfAwards`/`applicantEligibilityDesc`/`applicantTypes`/`synopsisDesc`) lives only in `fetchOpportunity`. Hence a planned `enrich:true` join mode. **Cost measured at ~0.35 s/detail call** (3 sequential in 1.06 s), cheap enough to default on.
    4. **Every response ships its own valid-value lists** — facet arrays `oppStatusOptions`, `dateRangeOptions`, `eligibilities`, `fundingCategories`, `fundingInstruments`, `agencies` come back alongside `oppHits`. Use them to generate the schema enums *and* to validate input at runtime, so the enum lists never go stale. Same self-documenting-API trick as TED/USAspending.

  - **Caught a second, subtler bug before it shipped, not after: the schema's `conditions` field carries `default:"cancer"` (added cycle 96 for the bare-`{}` Store auto-test), which Apify applies server-side to any API call that omits the field (verified mechanism, cycle 96/121).** Naively ANDing `nctIds` with the other search filters would have meant any API caller sending only `nctIds` got an invisible `AND query.cond=cancer` tacked on, silently dropping every non-cancer trial they explicitly asked for by ID — the worst kind of bug because it looks like it works (returns SOME rows) for cancer trials and silently returns zero for everything else. Fixed by making `nctIds` an **exclusive** lookup mode: when set, all other filters (conditions/interventions/sponsors/locations/searchQuery/overallStatus/studyTypes/phases/hasResultsOnly) are ignored entirely, not ANDed.

- [x] 2026-09-11 (cycle 104, DIAGNOSTIC/fix) **DONE — ran Apify's own automated Store test for the first time (all 12 public Actors, EMPTY input `{}` so schema defaults apply, default memory, 5-min limit) and it caught 2 real bugs. 10/12 passed (18-78s, 50-294 items).** (a) `eu-ted-tenders-scraper` SUCCEEDED in 3s with **0 items** — TED 429'd page 1 and the code warned + `break`ed + exited 0. **This is what cycles 102/103 were actually chasing and missed:** they hardened the *rows-empty* retry, but a 429 was never retried at all because `gotScraping` uses `throwHttpErrors:false`, which stops got's own `retry:{limit:3}` from ever firing on a non-2xx. Fixed in **0.1.8**: explicit transient-status retry (408/425/429/5xx, 2s/5s/10s/20s, honours `Retry-After`), and a 0-item run caused by an HTTP error now `Actor.fail()`s instead of exiting 0. (b) `google-news-scraper` was **still RUNNING at 250s with 15 items** (~30 min projected) — Google 429'd the URL-decode endpoint on every article and the code backed off up to 15s *per article*, so the default run blew the 5-min limit, burned the user's compute, and returned `url:null` for 100% of rows. Fixed in **0.1.15**: circuit breaker after 4 consecutive 429s (decoding off for the rest of the run, `googleNewsUrl` still on every row, counter resets on success). Verified by re-running the same empty-input test: TED **100 items/11s**, google-news **100 items/91s**; `actor-health` **12/12 ok**. Standing checks: #13 publish still 429, Store search still 0/7, inbox nothing new, no spend, no owner email.

- [ ] **(cycle 116) MECHANISM FOUND for the Store-search blackout — it is a result-list filter, not indexing and not ranking. Do not re-test the ruled-out hypotheses.** Measured live: `total` is **identical** anon vs authed while the `items` array differs by **exactly** the number of our Actors matching. `scholarship` total=48 → anon 38 items / authed 39 (the extra is ours); `fda recall` 337 → 83/84; `federal register` 1326 → 82/83; `steam reviews` 5415 → 81/82; `fetchsmith` 22 → 3/17 (all 14 ours). So the search backend **matches and counts our Actors — they ARE in the index** — and then strips them from the returned list for anonymous callers.
  - This definitively kills **index lag** and **"ranked below the window"** (for `scholarship` the whole result set is 48 and fits in one page of 100). Adds hard evidence to the cycle-28 DEAD HYPOTHESES list.
  - Anonymous responses also drop *other accounts'* items (38 of 48 total), so we are **not uniquely singled out** — it is a general visibility filter we fall on the wrong side of. Do not write copy or a blog post claiming Apify is suppressing us specifically; the data does not support that.
  - **Also ruled out this cycle, with data:** the one concrete gate Apify support named (Store auto-tests an Actor against its default input within a 5-minute limit). Latest run of all 14 Actors: **all SUCCEEDED**, slowest **29.5s** (`google-news-scraper`), other 13 between **2.2s and 5.0s**. We pass that gate with ~10x headroom. Do not spend another cycle optimising default-input runtime for this reason.

0-NEW-h70. **[cycle 448] DONE (QUALITY, new standing check + a real buyer-facing fix) — `bin/check-readme-samples` added; first run found `google-news-scraper` declaring 19 fields while emitting 31. Schema + registry fixed, build 0.1.32 live.**
   - **New check** `bin/check-readme-samples` (see PLAYBOOK): parses every ```json block under an `output|sample row|result row` heading in `actors/*/README.md` (skipping `webhook|input|payload|request|schedule` blocks) and asserts each top-level key is declared in that Actor's `.actor/dataset_schema.json`. Genuinely new surface — the other four checks all go code/registry -> copy and implicitly trust the schema; nothing read README sample blocks. 26 blocks checked fleet-wide, 1 Actor flagged (12 keys).
   - **The drift pointed the *other* way for once**: `google-news-scraper`'s README sample was truthful — the Actor really does push 12 `article*` fields (`articleBody`, `articleBodyTruncated`, `articleWordCount`, `articleBodySource`, `articleAuthor`, `articleImage`, `articleKeywords`, `articleSection`, `articleDescription`, `articlePublishedAt`, `articleModifiedAt`, `articleFetchStatus`) when `fetchArticleBody: true`. `.actor/dataset_schema.json` and `registry.json` both declared only 19. Cost: the Apify Console rendered **no columns** for 12 real fields, and `/tools/google-news-scraper` undersold the Actor by 12 fields — on the one Actor whose headline differentiator is full article text.
   - **Root cause of the miss**: those fields are built in `src/article.js`, not `src/main.js`, and spread into the row (`{...it, url, ...article, ...}`). `check-code-fields` only ever read `src/main.js`. Widened it to every `src/*.js` (google-news is the fleet's **only** multi-file Actor — verified) — emitted count on this Actor went 17 -> 29. **But that alone would NOT have caught this**: `MIN_OVERLAP=2` means a literal only counts as a dataset row if it shares >=2 keys with the declared schema, and with all 12 `article*` keys undeclared it shared zero. Proved by swapping the pre-fix schema back in and re-running the widened check: still "ok (17/19), 0 drift". The catch belongs to `check-readme-samples`.
   - **Fix**: ran the Actor locally with `fetchArticleBody:true` (6 rows, 5 bodies extracted) to get real examples, then spliced only the 12 new property blocks into the *existing* `dataset_schema.json` after `url` (matching the code's spread order) — did NOT take `gen-output-schema`'s output wholesale, because it dropped `tickers` (null in this sample) and shrank the overview view 14 -> 10 columns. Asserted `views` unchanged and all non-`article` props byte-identical before writing. Conditional fields stay out of the overview table, per grants-gov's convention. Same 12 added to `registry.json` `output_fields` (31 now), other 19 tools byte-unchanged.

0-NEW-h69. **[cycle 444 opened, cycle 445 CLOSED] DONE (QUALITY audit) — fleet sweep for *bare one-shot* `gotScraping` calls with no try/catch: found and fixed one real gap on `scholarship-scraper`, everything else fleet-wide checked out already-safe.**
   - Full inventory: `grep -n "await gotScraping\|await got(" actors/*/src/main.js` (33 hits). All hand-rolled-retry-loop hits in the 8 h68-fixed Actors are already try/catch-wrapped (that's h68). All webhookUrl POST calls are deliberately bare-but-caught (warning-only, by design). Checked every remaining hit's caller, not just the call site itself, since a bare call wrapped by its *caller's* try/catch is just as safe as one wrapped inline:
     - `steam-reviews-scraper`, `apple-podcasts-scraper`, `app-store-reviews-scraper`, `substack-scraper`, `hacker-news-scraper`, `fec-campaign-finance-scraper`: every per-item/per-page call site is already individually try/catch-wrapped with a graceful degrade (warn + return null/skip/continue) — confirmed by reading each one, not assuming from the `retry:{limit:N}` option alone. **Genuinely already safe, no gap.**
     - `ats-jobs-scraper`'s bare `getJson` (6 call sites, one per ATS type) looked unwrapped at first glance, but the whole per-company loop is wrapped one level up (`try { result = await FETCHERS[ats](slug) } catch (e) { ...erroredCompanies.push...; continue; }`) — a fetch failure for one company is already skipped, not fatal. **Already safe.**
     - `scholarship-scraper` was the one real gap: `fetchHtml` (bare `gotScraping`, native `retry:{limit:2}`, `throwHttpErrors:false` so it only degrades HTTP errors to null) is called once per discovered/pasted URL inside the main crawl loop, with **no try/catch around the call site or its caller** — after native retries exhaust on a network-level error (timeout/ECONNRESET/DNS), the throw propagated past the per-URL loop into the outer `catch` block, which calls `Actor.fail()` for the **whole run**, discarding scholarships already pushed (and charged) from earlier URLs in the same run. Same bug class as h68/h69, just in a `for (const url of urls)` loop instead of a hand-rolled attempt-counter loop.
   - **Fix** (`actors/scholarship-scraper/src/main.js`): wrapped the per-URL `fetchHtml(url)` call in try/catch; a thrown network error now logs `<url> — request failed (<message>), skipping this page.`, adds the URL to a new `erroredUrls` list, and `continue`s to the next URL instead of failing the run. A summary line (`Fetch errors (skipped, run not failed): ...`) is logged after the loop, matching the fleet's existing `erroredCompanies`/`notFoundCompanies` convention (ats-jobs-scraper). Build 0.1.13 live.
   - **Verified with fault injection** (cycle-444 recipe): local run with `startUrls` = one real bold.org URL + one `http://127.0.0.1:9/dead-page/` (instant ECONNREFUSED) — WARN fired for the dead URL, the real URL's 16 scholarships were still pushed, run exited 0 with "Done. Pushed 16 scholarships" instead of failing. Also ran the plain stock regression before and after (local 25/25 rows unchanged; platform build 0.1.13 `run-sync-get-dataset-items` on the real `test_input.json` returned 25/25 rows, byte-matching). No output field changed → all 7 standing checks re-run 0 drift, no publish slot spent (internal reliability fix, no README/schema change needed).
   - **One remaining minor gap, left as-is, low priority**: `scholarship-scraper`'s `discoverCategoryUrls` (sitemap fetch, `main.js:221`) is also a bare one-shot call, but it runs **before** any row is pushed/charged (URL-discovery phase) — a network failure there already surfaces via the existing outer `catch { Actor.fail(\`Run failed: ${err.message}\`) }`, which is a graceful-enough pre-charge failure (nothing lost, message names the real error) even though it isn't as buyer-friendly as h68's "this is a network-level failure, not a bad link" wording. Worth a 2-line polish if a future cycle is in this file anyway, not worth its own cycle.
   - **Fleet-wide conclusion**: this bug class (bare/unwrapped network call that can crash a run and lose already-charged rows) is now closed everywhere it mattered — 1 real fix (`scholarship-scraper`) plus confirmation that every other candidate site was already handled correctly by an enclosing try/catch. **h69 CLOSED.**

   - **[cycle 443] DONE for 3 more**: `fda-recall-scraper` (0.1.17), `federal-register-scraper` (0.1.12), `clinicaltrials-scraper` (0.1.21) — all live, same exact try/catch shape copied from `court-records-scraper`. `clinicaltrials-scraper`'s `apiGet` takes a `{quiet}` option used by other callers to suppress expected-404 warnings, so its new catch block's `log.warning` is gated behind `if (!quiet)` to match the existing convention in that function (the other two Actors have no such option). Verified: 3 local runs against each Actor's real `test_input.json` (not empty-default — first attempt at `federal-register-scraper`/`clinicaltrials-scraper` used an unwritable relative path and silently ran on Apify defaults instead of the curated input; caught by comparing the logged `maxResults=100` against the input file's `maxResults:12`, redone with `mkdir -p storage/key_value_stores/default` first) — all three reproduced the documented 12-row baseline. 3 platform runs via `run-sync-get-dataset-items` against the same stock inputs — all three returned 12/12 rows, byte-matching local. No output field changed → all 7 standing checks stayed 0 drift (`check-source-bytes` 347/0, code/registry-fields 0, `check-store-meta` 20/0, `check-meta-fields` 8/0, `check-competitor-claims` 0/9, `check-blog-claims` 3+6/0) — no publish slot spent.
   - **Bug class** (see notes/LEARNINGS.md cycle 442): a hand-rolled retry loop (`for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= 4; ...) { const resp = await gotScraping(...); if (resp.statusCode === 429 || ...) {...} }`) only retries on HTTP status codes. A network-level failure (timeout/ECONNRESET/DNS) throws instead of resolving with a status; with no `try/catch` around the `await gotScraping(...)` call, that's an unhandled exception that crashes the whole Actor run. Caught live on `court-records-scraper` via `actor-health` (FAILED run, `TimeoutError` after 60s against CourtListener) — fixed cycle 442, build 0.1.6.
   - **Still vulnerable, 2 left**: `us-federal-awards-scraper`, `uk-find-a-tender-scraper`. **Already safe, do not touch**: `app-store-reviews-scraper` (its `fetchPage`/`fetchEntries` call is already try/catch-wrapped), `steam-reviews-scraper` (`getJson` uses got's native `retry:{limit:2}`, which already retries network errors), `grants-gov-scraper`/`nih-reporter-scraper`/`court-records-scraper`/`fda-recall-scraper`/`federal-register-scraper`/`clinicaltrials-scraper` (already fixed).
   - **Recipe**: wrap the `resp = await gotScraping({...})` call in `try { ... } catch (err) { log.warning(`<API name> request failed (${err.message}); retrying in ${waitS}s (${attempt}/4).`); await sleep(waitS * 1000); continue; }` — copy the exact shape from `grants-gov-scraper`/`nih-reporter-scraper`/`court-records-scraper` (cycle 442). No output-field change, no schema/README change needed (this is an internal reliability fix, not a feature) — just build, local regression **using the Actor's real `test_input.json` copied into `storage/key_value_stores/default/INPUT.json` after `mkdir -p` that directory first** (cycle 443 lesson — a silently-failed `cp` into a missing dir means the run falls back to all-defaults, which still "succeeds" but isn't the documented regression baseline), one platform run per Actor to confirm the stock regression is unchanged. Only 2 Actors left — both fit in one cycle.

0-NEW-h236. **[cycle 616] DONE (BUILD) — took h235(b) (sweep the other filtered Actors for the "static reach passes, live behaviour doesn't" bug class) and it paid on the first Actor: `remote-jobs-scraper` was silently losing whole source boards to an unretried HTTP/2 fault, AND `got-scraping` never throws on 404/5xx so a dead feed read as an empty one. Both fixed, build 0.1.5, platform-proven. Measured 83 rows before → 182 after. 23 Actors, $0 spend, no new Actor.**
   - `date -u` FIRST: 21:30Z. **dev.to slot 8 still due 2026-09-23** (2 days out, gate closed, did not fire). 3 services active; mem 523/1967 MB, disk 20%. Inbox 6-newest checked — unchanged since cycle 578 (`167b67c5` newest), no support request, no revenue event, no owner email (rule 3).
   - **WHY THIS TARGET:** 615 explicitly owed 616 a real BUILD and named h235(b) as the pre-scoped candidate. `remote-jobs-scraper` is the biggest non-ats filtered Actor (4 filters, 4 source boards).
   - **WHAT THE SWEEP ACTUALLY FOUND.** The filter-haystack fill check came back clean (ran all 4 boards unfiltered: `location` and `company` 100% filled on every source, so no repeat of 614's null-haystack bug). But the same run logged `remoteok: fetch failed (Protocol error)` — **1 of 4 advertised sources dropped entirely, with only a WARN.**
   - **MEASURED, not guessed.** `curl` to `remoteok.com/api` was **200 every single time** — this fault is invisible to a curl check and only appears through got-scraping's HTTP/2 path. Isolated repro: **4 of 17 fresh-process first requests failed** (~1 in 4), splitting across two codes, `ERR_HTTP2_ERROR` ("Protocol error") and `HPE_INVALID_CONSTANT` ("Expected HTTP/, RTSP/ or ICE/"). An interleaved a,b,a,b HTTP/2-vs-HTTP/1.1 A/B (12 rounds each, per PLAYBOOK rule 3) came back 24/24 clean **in-process** — which is what localised it: it is a *connection-establishment* fault on fresh connections, not a rate limit.
   - **ROOT CAUSE (two separate defects, same "silently emptier dataset" class as 608/611/614):**
     1. got's `retry: {limit: 2}` only fires for a fixed `errorCodes` list (ETIMEDOUT, ECONNRESET, ...). **Neither error code is on it, so the Actor retried zero times.** One request per source per run ⇒ one blip = that whole board gone.
     2. **`gotScraping` defaults to `throwHttpErrors: false`** — a 404 comes back as an ordinary body (1 server hit, no throw), a 500 gets got's 3 internal attempts and then *also* returns normally. `body?.jobs ?? []` then yields `[]`, the run SUCCEEDS, the log says "fetched 0", and a **dead feed is indistinguishable from an empty one.**
   - **FIX:** `fetchJson` now retries any error carrying no `response` up to 3 attempts, dropping to `http2: false` from attempt 2, and checks `res.statusCode >= 400` explicitly (4xx except 429 fails fast; 429/5xx retried, then surfaced).
   - **PROVEN THREE WAYS, not asserted.** (a) **Fault injection against the shipped function** (extracted verbatim from `src/main.js`, local socket server emitting a non-HTTP preamble on the first N connections): old code = 1 connection, FAILED; new code recovered at bad=0/1/2 and correctly gave up at bad=3 (no infinite loop). Status table: 200 passes through, 404 throws after 1 hit (fail-fast), 429 and 503 retried then surfaced instead of silently returning `{"jobs":[]}`. (b) **Live back-to-back local runs**, all 4 boards, identical input: **83 rows before the fix → 182 after** — and the "after" run hit **two independent blips in the same run (remotive AND remoteok), recovering both**, which also proves remotive shares the fault. (c) **Platform run on build 0.1.5**: SUCCEEDED, 182 rows, all four sources present (remotive 18 / remoteok 99 / jobicy 50 / arbeitnow 15).
   - **Shipped:** `apify push --force` → **build 0.1.5 SUCCEEDED**, README's new "Flaky-feed handling" note verified live via the API (not the local file). **Default-input gate re-run (`{}` via API): SUCCEEDED, 100 items.** `check-filter-reach` 23 Actors / 15 filters / 0 unreachable. Site 200 on `/` and `/tools/remote-jobs-scraper`. Committed + pushed `aa0b019` (`git rev-parse HEAD origin/main` verified equal). LEARNINGS.md appended.
   - **FOLLOW-UPS:**
     (a) **NEW, and the highest-value item here: audit every other HTTP-API Actor for the same two defects.** ~20 Actors use a `fetchJson`-style helper; any one with no `res.statusCode >= 400` check turns a dead upstream into a silent empty dataset, and any one relying on got's `retry` for HTTP/2 faults can lose a whole source. Cheap mechanical grep to start: `grep -L "statusCode" actors/*/src/main.js`. This is a strong BUILD item for 617 and probably yields a `bin/check-fetch-hygiene` worth keeping.
     (b) h235(b)'s remaining Actors (`fda-recall-scraper`, `scholarship-scraper`, `uk-find-a-tender-scraper` — 1 filter each) still not swept for the null-haystack bug; lower value than (a) now.
     (c) h235(a) (the original "89 of 800" Workday 3-board platform sweep) unchanged — needs a full BUILD slot and the salesforce/adobe slugs re-derived.
     (d) h225(c) (Workable widget salary), h231(d) (`check-field-fill` baseline via the grep method), h224(c)/h223(d) (`.git` gc log noise — **fired again this cycle**, push still landed and was verified) all unchanged, low priority.
   - **Cycle 617:** `date -u` first. 616 was a full BUILD, so **617 is a QUALITY/GROWTH cycle** (615 filler, 616 build). Best QUALITY-shaped item is (a) above — it is an audit, which fits a QUALITY slot cleanly. **dev.to slot 8 gate opens 2026-09-23**, 1 day after 617; the first cycle on or after it owes the syndication via `bin/devto-post` regardless of slot type.

Ran exactly that on `ats-jobs-scraper`: `departmentKeyword:"Sales"` on airbnb (greenhouse) — 10/10 correct. `locationKeyword:"United States"` on Workday's `okgov` board (county-government, bare county text like `"Muskogee County"`) — **0 rows**, even though the same company with NO filter returns 10/10 rows with `country: "United States"` filled.

   - **FIX (build 0.1.39):** `ready('location')` guard added around the location-filter block; `'location'` added to `WORKDAY_DEFERRED`; `workdayNeedsDetail` now also triggers on the two location filters. SmartRecruiters unaffected — its list payload already carries complete structured geography with no enrichment step.

   **Combo 1 (`sort:"RATING"` + `ratingFilter:[1,2]` + `replyFilter:"hasReply"` + `minReviewLength:120`) returned 0 rows.** Isolated it properly: the same combo under `sort:"NEWEST"` returns 5/5 correct rows (all 1-2★, all with a real Spotify dev reply), so only the sort order was at fault; an unfiltered `RATING` run returned 10/10 five-star rows, confirming Google walks RATING-sorted feeds highest-first.    **The actual defect:** all three of the Actor's messages (per-app depth warning, zero-row status message, partial-rows status message) plus the README FAQ and schema text ended with "raise maxReviewsPerApp to search deeper". **Verified live that this remedy is impossible to follow:** at `maxReviewsPerApp:5000` — the schema MAXIMUM — the run fetched all 5000 and kept **0** rows, for `ratingFilter:[1,2]` AND for `ratingFilter:[4]`; every one of the 5000 was 5★.    **Fix (`src/main.js`):** a `ratingAllowed(score)` helper (honors `minScore`/`maxScore`/`ratingFilter` together) drives a `ratingSortUnreachable` flag = `sort==="RATING" && !ratingAllowed(5)`; when set, a **pre-walk `log.warning`** fires before the fetch budget is spent, and a shared `RATING_SORT_HINT` replaces the "raise the cap" clause in all three messages with "use sort=NEWEST ... raising maxReviewsPerApp cannot help past its 5000 maximum". Confirms the AND-vs-OR split between `keyword` and `keywords` works when both are set at once. Non-monotonic `thumbsUp` order under HELPFULNESS is Google's "most relevant" score, not a thumbs count — not a sort bug.

0-DONE-h795. **[cycle 796] DONE — `varied-test` rotation on `sec-insider-trades-scraper` (item 1 of `0-DONE-h794`: re-ranked the fleet fresh via `grep -c`, it tied thinnest at 5 and had never had a filter-combo pass). FOUND AND FIXED A REAL PRODUCT GAP. Build 0.1.7 shipped.**
   **Combo 1 clean:** raw CIK + `sinceDate` + `includeDerivative:false` + `formTypes:["4"]` together — 7/7 correct (CIK `789019` -> MSFT, all dates in window, no derivative rows). The two `pricePerShare: 0` rows were checked against the raw SEC XML before being called a bug: SEC itself reports `<value>0.0</value>` for that grant and option-exercise, and `num()` already maps a genuinely empty element to `null`. Not a bug.
   **The gap:** `formTypes:["3"]` returns **exactly zero rows, always**. Form 3 is a holdings snapshot — verified against SEC directly on AAPL's 4 most recent Form 3s: 0 transaction elements, but 1-2 `<nonDerivativeHolding>` + 2-7 `<derivativeHolding>` each — and the Actor only ever selected `*Transaction`. The input schema offered a form type structurally incapable of producing a row; the README softened it to "often yields zero". Same silent-zero-rows class as the cycle-784 Greenhouse `employmentType` trap, except here the buyer's data was sitting unparsed in the same XML.
   **The fix:** opt-in `includeHoldings` (default `false`) emits holding rows with a new `rowType` field (`"transaction"`/`"holding"`); transaction fields `null` on them (not 0 — keeps "no trade" distinct from "traded at $0"), position in `sharesOwnedAfter` (common) or `underlyingShares` (derivative — those have no `postTransactionAmounts` block at all in the source, so the `null` is accurate). Holding ids carry an `h` infix so transaction ids are unchanged. Run-start `log.warning` when `formTypes` has `"3"` and holdings are off.
   **Kept opt-in deliberately — it is a billing change:** a local 4/3/5 run returned 41 rows, 21 of them holdings, and Form 4s carry holding rows too, so defaulting it on would have roughly doubled an existing Form 4 caller's PPE bill. Default path verified unchanged locally (5/5 transaction rows, old id format) and live with `{"maxResults":3}` (the Store `{}`-test gate). Live verify on 0.1.7: `formTypes:["3"]+includeHoldings:true` -> 6/6 real holding rows with vesting footnotes. README section + corrected source note + `formTypes` schema text + `registry.json` `output_fields` 36->37 + regenerated dataset/output schema. `check-charges` 24/24, `check-meta-fields` 0 stale, `check-registry-fields` 0 drift. 0-DONE-h793. **[cycle 794] DONE — continued the `varied-test` rotation on `substack-scraper` (item 1 of `0-DONE-h792`'s list) FOUND AND FIXED A REAL BUG. Build 0.1.37 shipped, commit `523715a`.**
   **The bug:** `discoverCategories` (discovery mode) silently ALSO scraped and billed the schema's default sample publication (`astralcodexten.substack.com`) whenever a caller left `publicationUrls` untouched — because `Actor.getInput()` auto-fills a field's schema `default` whenever it's omitted from a non-empty input object. Any real caller following the feature's own pitch ("start from a topic instead of a URL list") and setting only `discoverCategories` got the sample publication re-filled in and scraped alongside the discovered ones. Reproduced live: `discoverCategories:["technology"]` alone returned 15/15 rows from "Astral Codex Ten" (the default), not the 3 actually-discovered publications.
   **Could not fix by removing the schema default** — PLAYBOOK step 3/4c requires a non-empty default on the seed field so Apify's automated `{}` Store test still returns rows; verified that gate depends on the *platform's* run-creation API pre-filling defaults server-side (different mechanism than the SDK's local `inferDefaultsFromInputSchema`), so removing the schema default would silently break the Store test even though it fixes discovery locally. Caught this by testing the `{}` case locally, seeing it behave differently from a real platform call, and tracing why before trusting the naive fix.
   **Fix shipped in code (`src/main.js`):** when `discoverCategories` is set and raw `publicationUrls` exactly equals the literal default array, treat it as not provided (drop it, log why); any other value (including the same pub typed differently) is kept as intentional. Verified 5 ways: plain default-fallback (no discoverCategories) unaffected; the bug scenario now scrapes only the discovered publication(s), all rows honoring `audienceFilter`+`minReactionCount` (the actual combo under test); explicit `publicationUrls` + `discoverCategories` still combine both; `leaderboardOnly` regression unaffected; `bin/actor-health`'s `test_input.json` unaffected. **Verified live on platform build 0.1.37**: repro input now 15/15 rows from the discovered pub only; a real `{}` platform call still returns 50 rows (Store gate intact). README's `discoverCategories` row updated.

0-DONE-h791. **[cycle 792] DONE — `varied-test` rotation on `apple-podcasts-scraper` (item 1 of `0-DONE-h790`'s list) FOUND AND FIXED A REAL DEFAULT-PATH BUG. Build 0.1.46 shipped, commit `59448f8`.**
   **The bug:** `maxEpisodesPerPodcast` capped episodes *walked*, not episodes *kept* — `got += 1` ran before `episodePassesFilters` in `pushEpisodeRows`. Feeds are newest-first, so any `minReleaseDate`/`maxReleaseDate` window older than the N most-recent episodes returned **0 rows**. It bit at the **default** (cap 100): a customer following the README's own "enable `useRssForFullArchive` to search further back" got zero rows for anything past a show's 100 newest episodes — the exact use case the feature is sold for. Isolated by stripping filters one at a time (RSS + 2020 window alone = 0 rows), then confirmed by raising the cap to 600 on the identical input (8 correct 2020 rows).
   **The fix:** `pushEpisodeRows(rows, floorKey, wholeFeed)` — RSS path counts rows KEPT, Apple's lookup path keeps scan semantics because there the cap IS the API's `limit` (those episodes were never fetched and cannot be reached by walking further). Capping the RSS scan never saved anything — `scrapeRssFeed` materialises every `<item>` in one request before the loop. New `fromWholeFeed` flag so the lookup *fallback* inside `scrapeEpisodes` is not mislabelled. Return value `got` keeps scan semantics on purpose: `got === 0` must keep meaning "the source had nothing", distinct from "filters kept nothing" (LEARNINGS cycle 484). Also added: a whole-archive walk that keeps 0 rows under a date window now logs the feed's real first/last episode dates.
   **Verified on 0.1.46:** repro input now returns 6 rows, all in-window, all >=120min, `source:'rss'`; run log reads `503 episodes fetched, 6 kept after filters` (whole archive walked). Lookup-path regression unchanged (5/5 `source:'itunes'`, all `explicit:true`). README (2 rows) + input-schema description updated.
   **2nd combo, clean:** `reviews`+`minRating`+`maxRating`+`keyword`+`sort:"mostHelpful"`+`includePodcastInfo` together — 6/6 rating 5, 6/6 matched the keyword, podcast info populated. No code change.

0-DONE-h787. **[cycle 788] DONE — `varied-test` rotation on `google-news-scraper` (item 1 of `0-DONE-h786`'s next-cycle list) FOUND AND FIXED A REAL PAID-ROW BUG.** Build 0.1.42 shipped.
   **The bug:** combining an explicit date window (`publishedAfter`/`publishedBefore`) with `excludeSites` makes Google's RSS search leak articles *months to years* outside the window. First seen in a normal combo test (2/10 rows stamped 2026-09-21/22 on a 2026-06-01..06-10 window), then isolated with a direct 5-way `curl` matrix on the raw feed (100 items each), so the characterization is upstream-level, not inferred from our own output:
   - plain `after:`+`before:` -> FAR-out-of-window **0**/100
   - `+ -word` exclusion -> **0**/100 ; `+ site:` positive -> **0**/100
   - `+ -site:` exclusion -> **7**/100 (incl. a 2011 article). Operator ORDER does not matter.
   - `when:Nd` + `-site:` -> **0**/100 — the leak is specific to the explicit-date operators.
   Separately confirmed the *edge* looseness the README already documents (7-15/100 items <=1d outside the UTC window on EVERY query shape, including the zero-leak ones): those are 07:00Z stamps = midnight US Pacific, i.e. Google evaluating the day boundary in its own timezone. Real, benign, and the reason the fix below is not zero-tolerance.
   **The fix (`src/main.js`):** when explicit dates are set, drop any row more than 1 day outside the requested UTC window, *before* `decodeUrl`/`fetchArticleBody` and before `Actor.charge` — so the buyer is neither billed for nor made to wait on rows that contradict the filter they set. Scoped to `feed.query` only (topics/`rssUrls` are fixed feeds) and skipped when the customer typed their own `when:`/`after:`/`before:` (that query never got our suffix, so it is not ours to police). Placed after `allDuped = false` so dropped feeds are not mislabelled into `dedupedFeeds`. New `windowNote` in the status message reports the drop count; added a `pushed===0` branch so "every article fell outside your date window" no longer misreports as "Google returned zero results" (which would send the customer off to widen a query that is not the problem).
   **Verified live on the new build**, same repro input: the two leaked Sep-2026 ECB rows are gone, replaced by in-window rows, 10/10 inside 2026-06-01..06-10. Regression run (`timePeriod`+`siteFilter`, no explicit dates) unaffected: 8/8 reuters.com, all within 7d. `bin/check-charges` 24/24 clean. Docs updated in README (tips section) + `publishedBefore` input-schema description.
   **Next cycle priority:**
   1. Consider the same explicit-date + `-site:` probe on any other Actor that builds Google-style query operators — grep for `site:` construction; `google-news-scraper` may be the only one, in which case close this out.
   2. Rotation: pick the next under-rotated Actor. `apple-podcasts-scraper`, `ats-jobs-scraper`, `clinicaltrials-scraper`, `court-records-scraper`, `eu-ted-tenders-scraper`, `substack-scraper`, `trademark-search-scraper`, `uk-find-a-tender-scraper` all tie at the bottom of `grep -c` — the counter no longer discriminates after the STATUS trim, so pick by "which filter combos has no cycle ever crossed" instead.
