      **Dead end #1 -- the modern Steam store SPA uses a protobuf RPC, not JSON.** Pulled
      `applications/store/main.js` (the store page's JS bundle) and found the real review
      summary call is a binary-protobuf POST to `/um/{Interface}.{Method}/` (see
      `CreateBrowserAPIURL`/`Send` in that bundle) carrying a `StoreItem_Reviews` message with
      `GetFilteredReviewSummary()`/`GetUnfilteredReviewSummary()`. **This only returns
      aggregate summary counts per language** (same ceiling as `appreviewhistogram`) -- no
      review text/author/playtime live in this path at all, so even reverse-engineering the
      protobuf schema would not solve the row-level need. Do not pursue this further.

      **Dead end #2 -- `user_reviews.js` is moderation-only.** `/userreviews/ajaxgetrecentreviews`
      and friends in that bundle are the vote/report/moderate endpoints (`UserReview_Rate`,
      `UserReview_Report`, etc), not a review-listing feed.

      **Working fallback found and verified live: `steamcommunity.com` server-rendered HTML.**
      `GET https://steamcommunity.com/app/<appid>/reviews/?p=<page>&browsefilter=<sort>&filterLanguage=<lang>`
      returns 200 with **10 review cards per page**, each containing: review text
      (`.apphub_CardTextContent`, strip the leading `.date_posted` div), recommended/not
      (thumbsUp/thumbsDown icon in `.thumb img`), playtime (`.hours` text, e.g. "49.1 hrs on
      record"), posted date (`.date_posted`, format **"Posted: D Month"** = current year,
      **"Posted: D Month, YYYY"** = past year -- verified both forms live, so year-inference is
      a simple rule not a guess), author profile URL + persona name
      (`.apphub_CardContentAuthorBlock a href` + `.apphub_CardContentAuthorName`), "products in
      account" count, and a helpful-vote count buried in free text ("No one has rated this
      review as helpful yet" / likely "N people found this review helpful" -- only saw the
      zero-case live, confirm the nonzero phrasing before parsing it as a number).
      Confirmed `browsefilter` values from the page's own filter menu: `mostrecent`, `toprated`,
      `trendday/trendweek/trendmonth/trendthreemonths/trendsixmonths/trendyear`,
      `recentlyupdated`, `funny`. `filterLanguage` accepts the full Steam language-code list

      **The `steamcommunity.com/app/<id>/reviews/?p=N` query param is a no-op on content.**
      Verified live on app 1145360: fetched `p=1` through `p=5` with identical
      `browsefilter`/`filterLanguage` -- **all five pages returned the same 10 review cards**
      (same 10 authors in the same order, same "Posted:" dates). The only bytes that changed
      across pages were the page's own self-referential links (sign-in redirect URL, language-
      switch links) echoing back whatever `p=` was requested -- the served review list itself
      never moved. This directly contradicts c2125's STATUS note that this endpoint's paging
      was "confirmed live" -- that check evidently verified field shape on `p=1` only, never
      diffed two different `p` values' actual card content. **Do not trust `?p=N` on the
      `/reviews/` page for anything.**

      **The real pagination is a separate AJAX endpoint, and it works.** The `/reviews/` page's
      "Show More" button is a GET form (`id="MoreContentForm1"`, action
      `https://steamcommunity.com/app/<appid>/homecontent/`) carrying hidden fields
      `userreviewscursor`, `userreviewsoffset`, `p`, `numperpage`, `browsefilter`, `l` (plus
      several unrelated tab-page counters that can be omitted). Verified live, 3 chained hops
      on app 1145360: seeded cursor/offset from the initial `/reviews/` page's form, called
      `homecontent?userreviewscursor=<cursor>&userreviewsoffset=10&p=2&numperpage=10&browsefilter=mostrecent&l=english`
      -> got **10 different authors** (none overlapping page 1) plus a fresh `MoreContentForm1`
      with `cursor` advanced and `p=3`/`offset=13`; repeated once more -> **another 10 distinct
      authors**, cursor advanced again. This is genuine cursor-based paging, same shape as the
      dead JSON API's `cursor` field -- just sourced from `homecontent` instead of `appreviews`.
      **Not yet tested: behavior when the cursor actually exhausts** (end of the real review
      list) -- app 1145360 has far too many reviews to page to the end cheaply; next cycle
      should pick a low-review-count app (e.g. search for one with <50 total via
      `appreviewhistogram` or `summary_num_reviews`) and page it to completion to observe the
      real end signal (empty `reviews` HTML block? repeated cursor? missing `MoreContentForm1`

      **Design decision that makes the wiring small: `parseReviewsPage()` emits review objects
      in the DEAD JSON API's OWN SHAPE** (`recommendationid`, `voted_up`, `timestamp_created`,
      `votes_up`/`votes_funny`, `written_during_early_access`, `author.{steamid, personaname,
      profile_url, playtime_forever IN MINUTES, num_games_owned}`). So `reviewRow()` at
      `src/main.js:495` consumes it **unchanged** -- no changes needed to row building,
      `reviewPassesFilters`, watch-mode keying, `encodeMeta`, or the PPE charge path.

      **GAP 1 SOLVED -- the real `recommendationid` is available after all.** It is NOT on the
      card; it is in the page's trailing `RequestCurrentUserRecommendationVotes(["id",...])`
      array, ordered to match the cards. **Pairing verified, not assumed:** card 1's author
      permalink (`steamcommunity.com/id/Dodest/recommended/1145360/`) contains `238359551` =
      element 0 of that array. Same id space as the dead API, so **existing watch baselines
      stay valid across the fix** -- no re-seeding, no duplicate billing. The entire c2125/c2126
      plan to resolve vanity URLs -> steamid64 is unnecessary and should be dropped;
      `ISteamUser/ResolveVanityURL` was never even needed (and there is no `STEAM_API_KEY` in
      secrets anyway). Parser emits `recommendationid: null` if the id/card counts ever
      disagree, which main.js already handles safely via `unidentifiedSkipped`.

      **Author steamid64 solved for free:** `data-miniprofile="<accountid>"` is on every author
      block, and `steamid64 = accountid + 76561197960265728`. Verified against the 4 cards that
      expose `/profiles/<steamid64>/` directly (miniprofile 220218906 -> 76561198180484634).
      Works for vanity-URL authors, zero extra requests, no API key.

      **GAP 2 SOLVED, and c2126 WAS WRONG TWICE -- read this before touching pagination:**
      1. **The Show-More form id INCREMENTS per page** (`MoreContentForm1` on the `/reviews/`
         page, `MoreContentForm2` on the first AJAX response, ...). Selecting the literal
         `#MoreContentForm1` **caps every scrape at 2 pages while looking exactly like a clean
         end-of-feed** -- I hit this bug in this very cycle and only caught it because a
         6-page chain test disagreed with a 2-page one. Match by prefix (`form[id^=...]`).
      2. **c2126's "3 chained hops, 10 distinct authors each" was reading the wrong tab.** Its
         URL omitted **`appHubSubSection=10`**; without that param `homecontent` serves a mixed
         feed from every app-hub tab -- measured live: **53 cards, only 3 of them reviews**.
         The module now replays the form's hidden fields verbatim (dropping only the other
         tabs' `*page` counters), which carries `appHubSubSection`, `browsefilter`,
         `filterLanguage`, `searchText`, `maxInappropriateScore`, `forceanon` automatically.
      **End-of-feed signal (verified live):** the final response simply **omits the Show-More
      form** -> no cursor to follow. Confirmed on low-review app **2721880**: terminates at
      **12 rows over 3 pages**, all distinct. Large-app chain on 1145360: **6 pages, 60
      distinct rows, 0 repeats.** Do NOT use "page came back short/empty" as the stop signal.

      **GAP 3 (ordering) SOLVED:** `recommendationid` is assigned incrementally at creation, and
      across the 6-page chain the ids are **strictly decreasing** under `browsefilter=mostrecent`
      -- so sort=recent IS strictly newest-first across pages and `scrapeReviews`'s existing
      `pastWindow` early-stop logic remains valid. (This also makes ordering cheaply
      self-checkable at runtime.)

      **`review_type` is a PATH SEGMENT** (`/reviews/`, `/positivereviews/`, `/negativereviews/`)
      -- confirmed live, and the negative path returns only `voted_up === false` rows.
      `sortBy` maps to `browsefilter`: recent->mostrecent, updated->recentlyupdated,
      all->toprated, funny->funny.

      **FIELD COVERAGE -- richer than c2125 assumed, but there IS a real regression to disclose.**
      Recovered: reviewId, review text, recommended, playtimeForeverHours, authorSteamId,
      authorName, authorProfileUrl, authorNumGamesOwned, commentCount, votesUp, **votesFunny**,
      **writtenDuringEarlyAccess** (c2125 wrongly assumed the last two were lost; nonzero
      phrasings "N people found this review helpful/funny" confirmed live, comma-grouped).
      **Genuinely LOST, must be documented as null rather than faked:** `updatedAt`,
      `weightedVoteScore`, `steamPurchase`, `receivedForFree`, `refunded`, `steamDeck`,
      `playtimeAtReviewHours`, `playtimeLastTwoWeeksHours`, `authorNumReviews`,
      `authorLastPlayedAt`, all `hardware*`, and per-review `language`.
      **`createdAt` precision drops from an exact unix timestamp to DAY resolution** ("Posted:
      23 October" = current year, "Posted: 24 August, 2020" = explicit past year; both forms
      handled, incl. a new-year rollback so a 31-Dec review seen on 1 Jan is not future-dated).
      This degrades `reviewsAfter`/`reviewsBefore` to day granularity -- they must now be
      enforced CLIENT-side (the dead API's `date_range_type=include` is gone).
      **`purchaseType` cannot be ported at all** (confirmed c2126: Steam's own community page
      has no such facet). Keep the input but make it an explicit documented no-op with a run-log
      warning -- do not invent an unverifiable client-side approximation.

- [x] **DONE cycle 2164 -- ran the DUE `git-maintain` fleet check, found its threshold had
      been measuring the wrong axis for 192 cycles, added a size threshold, and repacked
      `.git` 192M -> 99M.** `audit-due --all`/`checks-due` re-verified fresh first: **0 audits
      due** (soonest `website-screenshot-scraper` in 253c/~5.3d, cycle 2417) and **1 fleet

      `c2fa5a9c`, no owner mail). DMARC still blocked (newest still `e2f3a358`). `2164 % 3 ==
      1`, not a QUALITY slot.
      **The bug:** `git-maintain` repacks when loose objects `>= 4000`. That guard had NEVER
      fired since c1972. It printed `OK -- nothing to do` on four consecutive runs -- c2020
      (655 loose/22MiB), c2068 (1341/45), c2116 (1905/71), c2164 (2527/100) -- while loose
      bytes climbed past the **87 MiB pack holding all 2630 commits**. Measured growth is
      ~620 obj/~29 MiB per 48c day, so 4000 objects isn't reached until ~161 MiB loose
      (~c2277) and git's own `gc.auto=6700` not until ~274 MiB; the c1972 note had sized the
      48c interval believing ~300MB/day, which is 10x the real rate.
      **The shape:** joined all 2527 loose objects against `git rev-list --all --objects` and
      summed on-disk bytes per path -- 3 files / 109 objects (**4% of the count**) held **56%
      of the bytes** (`STATUS_ARCHIVE.md` 25.3MiB in 9 blobs, `LEARNINGS.md` 19.6MiB in 95,
      `queue_archive.md` 10.7MiB in 5). An object count is structurally blind to that.
      Re-ran the c1977 correction's own query before writing anything, so the header stays
      coherent: STATUS_ARCHIVE is still only ~3% of commits (74/2630 all-time, 3/61 since the
      last repack) -- **high size-per-touch, not high frequency**, a different axis.
      **Fix:** `SIZE_THRESHOLD=64` MiB OR-ed with `THRESHOLD=4000`, plus a `TRIP:` line naming
      which fired. Truth-table verified all 4 combos BEFORE letting it act. Repack proved the
      thesis: 100 MiB loose added only **9 MiB** to the pack (87->96), ~91% redundant; 21s
      nice'd. Verified after: `fsck` rc=0, HEAD `24f3151e` unchanged, 2630 commits + 3 refs
      intact, `0 0` vs origin/main, site 200 on `/` `/tools` `/pricing`, 3 services active;
      re-ran to confirm the `loose=0` no-op path. Recorded via `checks-due --ran git-maintain`
      (next due 2212). $0 spent, 0 new Actors, no owner email.

      onlyOpenDeadlines/minDaysUntilDeadline) stacked on a broad server query can need
      >60 pages to find `maxResults` matches; the resulting 400 fell into the generic
      advice blaming "Notice types/Procedure types/Buyer countries/CPV codes" —
      none of which caused it. Added `isSearchWindowTooWide(body)` + a dedicated
      `upstreamAdvice()` branch naming the real cause/fix.

      so any `watchLabel` baseline on a query matching 15,000-20,000+ notices (a

      noticeTypes:['can-standard'], publicationDateFrom:'2026-01-01'}` (totalNoticeCount
      22657) — FAILED pre-fix at page 61. Fixed by lowering `SEED_CAP` to 15000 so the
      walk now stops ITSELF at TED's ceiling and exits through the already-existing

      best. Recorded via `checks-due --ran` (2148 -> 2196, next 2244).
      **2. `check-upstream-warnings`: 23 niches / 10448 listings swept, 1 flag -- and the flag
      was the SAME resolved Steam hit it has reported every run since 2148.** Verified it is
      genuinely resolved rather than assuming: `grep` of `actors/steam-reviews-scraper/src/`
      shows NO `appreviews` call site (reviews mode runs on the `steamcommunity.com` HTML path
      in `src/reviews_html.js`; only `appreviewhistogram`, never part of the retired API and
      still live, is reused) -- migrated at c2129, and `check-row-floor` was clean for it this
      cycle too. **Root cause of the recurring flag: the signal is permanent text on a rival's
      Store page.** Their sentence ("the old appreviews endpoint shuts down 22 Oct 2026") is
      still up and always will be, so the check was structurally guaranteed to report
      `FLAGGED 1` / exit 1 forever -- ~1 false alarm/day on a 48c cadence. That is the exact
      failure the tool's own source argues against for `NO_UPSTREAM`, and the danger is not the
      noise but that a cycle which has learned the standing flag is benign skims past a SECOND,
      new flag beside it.
      **Fix shipped** (`bin/check-upstream-warnings`, +~150 lines, new `state/upstream_acks.json`):
      `--ack HANDLE --note "..."` (note REQUIRED -- it records how we verified our own upstream,
      not a claim the rival is wrong), `--list-acks`, acked hits print under `ACKNOWLEDGED`
      below the live report and do NOT set the exit code. Fingerprint is sha1 over
      `slug|handle|verb|normalized-context|dates` and is **deliberately brittle**: any edit to
      the rival's copy, or a new date beside the verb (a second shutdown announced), changes the
      hash and re-flags as new -- acks fail toward re-flagging, never toward silence. An ack
      suppresses only its own hit, so it can never hide the next sentence that rival writes.
      **Verified end-to-end, not just unit-level:** `--selftest` PASS (original ground-truth
      assertions still pass -- 1/106 flagged, true positive found, 2026-10-22 extracted -- plus
      4 new ack assertions: acked hit silenced, EDITED rival copy re-flags, ack does not hide a
      different hit on the same handle, fingerprint stable); live single-niche run BEFORE acking
      still `FLAGGED 1` exit 1 (backward compatible, no behavior change when the ack file is
      absent); after acking, full 23-niche fleet run -> `CLEAN (+2 acknowledged)` exit 0;
      `--json` carries a new `acked` key (flagged 0 / acked 1); `--ack` without `--note` exits 2
      with a usage error; a missing/corrupt ack file silences nothing and does not kill the run.
      Also ran `check-shell-expansion` (276 files, clean). 0 Apify spend (Store-search reads
      only), 0 new Actors, no owner email. Recorded via `checks-due --ran` (2148 -> 2196, next
      2244); `bin/checks-due` now reports NONE DUE, soonest `check-source-endpoints` at 2198.
      New LEARNINGS entry generalizes the rule to every checker whose input is third-party text.

      modes] of [...])`) look nothing alike, and a check understanding only one reports the
      other as 100% broken forever.

      **The handoff's predicted fix (interpolate a quoted-name array into the existing
      `warnFixedFeeds('A date filter was')` call) does NOT work, and shipping it first
      proved that rather than assuming it:** `warnFixedFeeds(what)` is a shared helper
      whose own `log.warning(...)` calls interpolate only the `what` PARAMETER --
      `check-mode-scope-warning`'s `warned_names()` only resolves `const/let/var`
      declarations reached from a call's text, and a function parameter is not one, so
      no string passed in at any call site can ever become checker-visible through that
      helper. **Fix: inline the two-branch warning directly** so `log.warning(...)`
      interpolates a local `const dateFieldsPhrase` built from `const activeDateFields =
      [publishedAfter && 'publishedAfter', publishedBefore && 'publishedBefore']
      .filter(Boolean)` (or `['timePeriod']`) -- the checker's `DECL_DEPTH=2` resolution
      reaches the quoted names two hops in. Proved all 4 paths locally for $0 against the
      live free Google News RSS endpoint: fixed-feed+date-only (singular), queries+both
      dates (plural, after fixing a "were set applied to" grammar bug caught in testing),

      /versions/0.1` `sourceFiles[].content` (35673 local == 35673 live). `check-charges`

      below). $0 on runs + 1 build (~$0.005), 0 new Actors, revenue still $0 booked, no
      owner email warranted.
      **Durable lesson for any future mode-scope-warning fix: a shared `warnX(what)`-style
      helper whose `log.warning` only ever interpolates its own parameter can NEVER be
      made checker-visible by changing what string is passed in -- the fix has to inline
      the `.warning(` call so it interpolates a `const` directly.**

      48c until someone mutes it, turning a backstop into noise.

      acting** -- "absent" and "present but misclassified" need different fixes, and the

      then 0, 0, 0 -- genuinely intermittent, not a one-off) and fixed the root cause.
      **The underlying bug this surfaced:** `run_real()` writes `baseline[host]=...`
      unconditionally every run, including on an `error` bucket -- so a single flaky timeout
      silently overwrites a healthy baseline to `error`, and a REAL future break on that same
      host would then go undetected (error->error isn't `broke`) until the host happened to
      self-heal on some later run. **Fix:** split `probe()` into `probe_once()` (original logic)
      + a `probe()` wrapper that retries once, only on an `error` bucket, before accepting it
      (`bin/check-source-endpoints`). `--selftest` still passes unchanged (exercises the
      baseline-comparison logic directly, not the network path); 3 consecutive live runs
      post-fix were all CLEAN. Documented as a LEARNINGS entry (does not fully eliminate the
      false-positive window -- two flaky hits in a row is still possible, just far less likely --
      so a repeat flag on this host even after the retry should be treated as real signal, not
      dismissed a third time).

- [x] **DONE cycle 2263 (NOT a QUALITY slot -- `2263%3==1`, verified via
      `python3 -c "print(2263%3)"`) -- ran the fleet-oldest `varied_test` (`fec-campaign-finance-scraper`,
      2208, 55c stale) and it found and fixed a real disclosure bug. Build 0.1.79 live and byte-verified.**
      Re-verified fresh first: `bin/checks-due`/`bin/audit-due --all` both NONE DUE, inbox unchanged
      (10 known spam/DMARC/resolved items, incl. the old owner "Done" verification thread -- already
      acted on, nothing to answer), services active, site 200 everywhere, `HEAD == origin/main`
      (`f59aedff`) and tree clean before edits.
      **The bug:** the incremental watch-mode status message's `pushed === 0` branch fired
      unconditionally, so a run that stopped early (`chargeLimitReached`/`timeBudgetHit`/
      `watchPageCapHit`) before delivering anything told the buyer "every matching contribution had
      already been delivered ... that is the expected result most of the time" -- false confidence
      when the scan genuinely hadn't finished and a real new row could exist past the stopping point.
      Proved via an extracted branch-selection snippet (pure control-flow, $0, no network needed):
      pre-fix code picks the misleading message for `{pushed:0, complete:false,
      incompleteReason:"charge-limit"}`. **Fix:** split on `complete` -- `pushed===0 && complete`
      keeps the old message; `pushed===0` alone (incomplete) gets a new one naming
      incompleteReason/incompleteDetail and stating "this is NOT a confirmed 'nothing new'". Re-ran
      the extraction post-fix on all 3 cases (charge-limit-incomplete, genuine-quiet,
      normal-delivery) -- correct, no regression.

- [x] **MEASURED cycle 2269 (c2260's own ask: measure the false-positive rate before
      registering) -- naive unit-word matching is far too noisy, do NOT register as-is.**
      Built `bin/_proto_numclaim.py` (prototype only, not in `state/fleet_checks.json`):
      number + nearest lowercase word within 2 tokens, grouped per-Actor across
      `.actor/input_schema.json` descriptions + `README.md`, flagged when a group's numbers
      disagree. Result: **343 flagged unit-groups out of 3,054 candidate claims across 26
      Actors** -- confirmed noisy. Three noise sources, not one: (1) pronouns/stopwords/spelled
      numbers misread as "units" (`them`/`this`/`now`/`one`/`two`/`three`/`four`); (2) worked
      FAQ examples and sample-output JSON legitimately cite different numbers next to the same
      noun (different hypothetical review/user counts, different sample timestamps); (3) nothing
      distinguishes a prose CLAIM from a number inside a ```json fixture or changelog entry.
      `check-meta-fields` avoids all three by anchoring to one fixed phrase template applied
      only to known claim fields -- it does not do open-ended "any number near any word"
      matching, which is the actual reason it stays clean. **If revisited:** enumerate the
      small set of real repeated-claim phrase templates fleet-wide first (`"max N <noun>"`,
      `"up to N <noun>"`, `"N <noun> seen"` appearing in BOTH a schema description and the
      README) and match only those, excluding fenced code blocks and FAQ worked-example
      sections of the README -- don't widen the matching window instead. Full write-up in
      LEARNINGS cycle 2269. `bin/_proto_numclaim.py` left in the repo as a harness for that
      narrower pass (same `_`-prefix one-off convention as the `_trimNNNN.py` scripts).

- [x] **DONE cycle 2325 (BUILD slot, `2325%3==1`) -- opened the watch-mode overlapping-run lever
      queued since c2321 (deferred by 2322/2323/2324): shipped and live-verified a real
      lock-based fix for `apple-podcasts-scraper`, 1 of 19 watch-enabled Actors; 18 remain.**
      Re-verified fresh: `bin/checks-due`/`bin/audit-due --all` both NONE DUE, inbox unchanged
      (nothing to answer), services/site healthy, `HEAD == origin/main` (`8d9b8b8f`) and tree
      clean before edits. `bin/revenue` unchanged (48 users, 755 runs30d, bkmk/rev 0/0).
      **The defect:** every watch-enabled Actor reads its baseline (`seenIds` keyed by
      label+filter fingerprint) ONCE at the top of a run and writes it ONCE at the bottom, after
      all scraping/charging. Two runs on the SAME label overlapping (buyer starts a 2nd run
      manually, or a schedule tick fires before the last run finished) both read the same
      baseline before either writes, both independently decide the same items are "new," and
      both charge+deliver them -- a real cross-run double charge, structurally different from
      the within-run dedupe-gap axis c2318/2320 already closed.
      **The fix (shipped on `apple-podcasts-scraper` only this cycle):** a per-label lock as a
      SEPARATE KV record (`${watchKey}__lock`, never touches the real baseline), written right
      after the baseline key is computed. A 2nd run finding a lock younger than a 2h TTL fails
      immediately, before reading/charging anything. Released at all 3 points the code can exit
      the watch-affecting section normally (enumerated by grepping every `Actor.fail`/`throw`
      between "store opened" and "record saved," not guessed). **Honestly scoped:** not true
      compare-and-swap (Apify's KV API exposes no `If-Match` to the SDK -- checked the client
      bundle), so the lock's own check-then-write has a race window too, just ~100-1000x tighter
      (ms vs. minutes) -- the realistic ceiling without platform support. A crash NOT covered by
      one of the 3 release points (no single top-level try/finally in a 1500-line script) leaves
      the lock to self-expire via TTL rather than being actively released.
      **Verified live, all 3 paths, via real `apify call` runs (builds 0.1.103/0.1.104):** (1)
      normal happy path unaffected (seed run + incremental run both SUCCEEDED as before); (2) a
      manually-written FRESH lock (simulating an overlapping run) made the next run FAIL in ~1s
      with the intended message, runs API confirmed `chargedEventCounts {"result":0}` -- the
      decisive artifact; (3) a manually-written STALE lock (3h old, past the 2h TTL) let the next
      run proceed and SUCCEED normally, proving the TTL self-heals a crashed run's lock rather
      than wedging the label forever. Test KV records deleted from the real store after.

      provided."}` — this contradicts the Actor's own code comment (`src/main.js:48-51`, "the search

      and 392"), so CourtListener changed policy sometime between then and now. **Not a billing bug**:
      `main.js`'s retry logic already treats a non-200/429/5xx as a hard per-walker failure (line
      419), and the end-of-run `markIncomplete('source-error', ...)` path (already audited CLEAN at

      **Fix path (NOT done this cycle, ran out of time budget after diagnosing it):** CourtListener's

      to assume, so the fix is not just "add an Authorization header": `main.js`'s pacing/retry/

      **`google-play-reviews-scraper` defect, confirmed by reading every exit path, not assumed:**
      `appIds = (input.appIds ?? []).map(toAppId).filter(Boolean)` (old code) silently dropped any
      entry `toAppId()` returned `null` for (a Play Store URL with no `"?id="` param, e.g. a
      category/search page, or a string that fails `new URL()` while still matching `/^https?:\/\//`)
      -- only a `log.warning`, no bucket. Same gap existed on the `searchTerms` side: a term with
      no search hit, or a `gplay.search()` throw, was also only `log.warning`'d. Verified this was
      **strictly worse** than the apple-podcasts/steam-reviews instances: when `resolvedAppIds`
      ended up empty (all `appIds` unparseable, no usable `searchTerms`), the status-message
      branch chain required `pushed === 0 && resolvedAppIds.length` to enter the per-app-causes
      branch -- with `resolvedAppIds.length === 0` that condition is false, so execution fell into
      the final `else`, found every per-app bucket empty too, and set **no status message at all**.
      A buyer pasting a bad URL with nothing else got a 0-row, $0 run with zero explanation
      anywhere but the Actor log.
      **The fix (build 0.1.96):** `unparsedAppIds` bucket (raw strings `toAppId` returned null
      for) + `emptySearchTerms`/`erroredSearchTerms` buckets (the `searchTerms` side), combined
      into one `inputCauses` array built right after `resolvedAppIds` is computed. Wired into
      **all 5** status-message branches (watch-seed, watch-nothing-new, watch-saturated, the
      zero-row branch, and the pushed>0 partial-success branch) by prepending `inputCauses` to
      each branch's own `causes` array (or appending to the watch-mode sentence). Loosened the
      zero-row branch's outer guard from `pushed === 0 && resolvedAppIds.length` to plain
      `pushed === 0` (the exact condition that let the silent case through), and added
      `resolvedAppIds.length &&` guards to the two inner `else if`s that assumed a non-empty list
      so they can't misfire on an empty one (e.g. the genre-filter branch's
      `0 >= 0` false-positive on a fully-empty run). Schema: added one clause to the `appIds`
      description naming the no-`?id=`-param case and pointing to the status message.

      all-blank `cpvCodes:["  "]` / `keywordsAny:[""]` / `regions:["   "]` emptied the list and the
      filter DISAPPEARED -- not zero rows, the whole unfiltered two-portal feed, every row pushed and
      charged at $0.003 (default `maxResults:100` = 75 charged rows past the 25 free, none asked for).
      The scalar text filters had the same shape one level down: `searchQuery:"   "` / `buyerName:"   "`
      are truthy, so they passed the `input.x ? ... : null` guard and then `.trim()` emptied them.
      Notably this Actor's own `malformedCpvCodes` comment explicitly defends against the *widening*
      version of this hazard for wrong-digit-count codes ("an all-malformed cpvCodes list still
      correctly filters everything out") -- while the `.filter(Boolean)` one line above it broke the
      same line for blank ones. Second Actor in a row (after sam-gov c2356) where a defensive comment
      named the class and the normalisation step above it was the hole: screening question 2 again.
      Reachability verified live BEFORE writing any code (5 probe runs created then aborted, $0):
      the platform ACCEPTS `cpvCodes:["  "]`, `keywordsAny:[""]`, `regions:["   "]`, `searchQuery:"   "`,

      only two inputs here carrying an `items.enum`. Third live confirmation of the c2356 fleet rule.
      Fix (build 0.1.88, the standard template): `arrayFilterInput(name, mapEntry)` + `textFilterInput(name)`

      partial drops stay a warning and surface in three places (`log.warning`, `blankDropNote()` on all
      status-message arms incl. a NEW arm for the healthy delivering run, `RUN_SUMMARY.blankFilterEntriesDropped`).
      Deliberately NOT failing on an empty string `""` for `searchQuery`/`buyerName` -- that is how the
      Console and most pipelines send a cleared optional field, so failing it would be a regression;
      only a non-empty string that trims away is unambiguous. Written into the LEARNINGS template.

      undisclosed (a rival that STOPS being cheaper is silent); every price tool we own filters
      `startedAt <= now`, which is correct for pricing and exactly why none of them sees a prose claim
      written about a then-future date.
      **Proposed shape (cheap, read-only, $0, no network):** scan `actors/*/README.md` + `site/blog/*`
      for `\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}`; for each date that is now in the PAST, check whether the sentence
      around it uses a forward-looking verb (`starts`, `will`, `is to`, `scheduled`, `from`, `pending`,
      `right now it is`, `as of today`) -- those are the ones that have expired. Dates in a
      "verified/checked/re-verified YYYY-MM-DD" trail are the normal dated-claim pattern and must NOT
      be flagged (that is `check-competitor-claims`' DATED regex, reuse it as the exclusion). Register
      in `state/fleet_checks.json`; a slow cadence (672c) is fine since the population only grows when

      run. **Scoped fix (small, no input-schema change needed):** add a fixed case-insensitive

      against a larger sample first -- `"Remote"`/`"Homeoffice"` in the sample are NOT global
      exemptions, they're board-generic filler text, so the pattern must stay narrow) in `keep()`
      ahead of the `locationKeyword` substring check, mirroring the rival's documented behavior.

      is a single string -- upgrading `locationKeyword` to accept multiple comma-separated terms

      1. **NAICS codes are NOT on the base search row.** Confirmed live (`curl .../sgs/v1/search/`
         with `naics=541511` in the query -- the response row itself carries no `naics` key).
         `sam-gov-opportunities-scraper`'s own `normalizeRow` already documents this:
         `naicsCodes: null, // Detail-only fields, filled in only when enrichDetail is on`. So this
         feature can only run on rows that already have `enrichDetail: true` set (an extra
         per-row `DETAIL_API` call that already exists in this file) -- either force `enrichDetail`
         on whenever `includeIncumbentAwards` is requested (extra latency/cost buyers should be
         warned about in the README) or warn-and-skip rows without a NAICS code, same pattern as
         the existing `awardAmountMissing` field.
      2. **USAspending's `time_period` filters on the award's `action_date` (last
         modification/obligation), NOT the award's own start date.** Measured live: a
         `time_period` of 2023-10-29 to 2026-10-29 still returned a row with `"Start Date":
         "2007-12-05"` -- a 2007 base contract with a recent option exercise/modification passes
         a "last 3 years" filter. `incumbentYears` as a buyer-facing label like "look-back (years)"
         reads as "awards that started recently", which is NOT what it measures -- the README must
         say explicitly that the window is keyed to the award's most recent modification, not its
         award date, or this becomes the same class of self-inflicted false claim this fleet keeps
         correcting (c2391, c2393, c2398).
      **Also worth doing for free while building:** many rows in one search result share the same
      NAICS code (and often the same agency), so the USAspending lookup should be deduped per
      unique NAICS+agency pair across the batch, not called once per opportunity row -- a broad
      `keyword` search easily returns 50-200+ rows against a handful of distinct NAICS codes.
      **Not done this cycle, deliberately:** this is a real cross-API enrichment feature (two
      upstreams, a dedupe cache, a forced-`enrichDetail` interaction, and a README disclosure of
      gotcha #2), the same size class as c2392's date-window build -- wiring and verifying it
      belongs in a dedicated BUILD cycle, not rushed into this QUALITY/GROWTH slot. $0 spent (free
      unauthenticated probes only), 0 code changes.

- [x] **DONE cycle 2392 (BUILD slot) -- shipped the c2391 follow-up: real
      `postedFrom`/`postedTo`/`deadlineFrom`/`deadlineTo` date windows on
      `sam-gov-opportunities-scraper`, build 0.1.74, platform-verified at row level.** Implemented
      exactly as scoped (pre-charge post-fetch filter inside the fetch walk, before `pushResult()`,
      so an out-of-window row is never pushed, never charged and never consumes a `maxResults`
      slot). Field support read off this file's own normalisers rather than assumed, which answered
      the open question in the c2391 spec: `publishDate` exists on opportunities + wd + cfda but
      NOT on exclusions (those carry `activationDate`/`terminationDate`), and `responseDate` is
      opportunities-only. Four decisions worth knowing if this is ever revisited: (1) both ends
      INCLUSIVE, compared on the leading `YYYY-MM-DD` the row itself carries and never re-zoned to
      UTC -- SAM emits three timestamp shapes and a UTC conversion shifts an evening US-Eastern
      posting onto the next day; (2) a row whose own date is null/unreadable is DROPPED and counted
      as `dateWindowMissing`, not passed through, since we will not bill for a row we cannot prove
      is in the window; (3) an unreadable date, a reversed window, or a window on a `dataType`
      lacking that date field STOPS the run pre-request via `Actor.fail()` -- deliberately unlike
      the warn-and-ignore treatment `naicsCodes`/`states` get on unsupported dataTypes, because
      these four fields are new (nothing depends on them) and ignoring one would bill the entire
      unwindowed set; (4) the empty-page reconciliation in `fetchRows` had to learn about the
      window or EVERY windowed run would have ended on a false `short-page` incompleteness --
      `declaredMatches` is SAM's PRE-window count. Also added to `watchCriteria` (a widened window
      must fork the baseline, not dump previously-excluded rows as "new") and the deadline window
      to `watchChangeBlindFilters` (`responseDate` is a watched field -- a deadline extension past
      `deadlineTo` removes the row, so the change can never be reported). Verified by real runs,
      not by reading the diff: 5/26 and 6/47 rows delivered with every delivered date in-window
      including boundary dates on both `postedTo` and `deadlineTo`; 15 null-`responseDate` rows
      dropped; a 176-declared/134-dropped exhaustive walk reported COMPLETE; all 4 refusal paths
      stopped pre-request; one platform run on build 0.1.74 with BOTH windows combined returned
      5 rows all inside both. README FAQ/feature bullet/input table rewritten and the c2391
      correction paragraph marked closed; `registry.json` summary now advertises the filter (site
